score.method:
Per name:
    mu_ens = m + tilt + a   (tilt = EPS-revision tilt from conviction.py, 2026-10-08)
    m  = options-market part: conviction.py mu_market (T-bill + beta x ERP on the options-implied distribution).
    a  = research alpha = multiplier x w_llm x (r_research - m), where
         r_research = average of the agents' 12M mean return (supervisor ladder) and the reconciled fair value's return,
         w_llm      = the research weight in combine.py (33%),
         multiplier = conviction.py's shrink, clip(t / median t, 0.5, 1) (upper clip 2 until Kilian's 2026-10-20 card 'Cap at 1x'), t = |agents vs market| / sqrt(disp^2 + 10%^2).
    Open supervisor flags halve a; a thesis-break or fact-check flag blocks the name (score shown, no buy).
    score = gain in book Sharpe at the name's best share count (0..cap, exhaustive) against the live book at cost plus the
            committed buys (portfolio.json sharpe_combo), every name at mu_ens, riskcal correlations, same Sharpe formula as
            allocate.py (invested dollars, cash left out). Caps: stop budget, cash after committed
            buys. Would buy = score > 0 and a free name slot (cap 10).

portfolio.method:
Since 2026-09-29 (Kilian: "solve as one portfolio against the factor model") all candidates are sized together:
    maximize sum_i w_i (mu_i - rf) - (gamma/2) w' Sigma w,   gamma = 4 (quarter Kelly),
with w the share of total wealth (current account + new cash), mu_i the conviction-adjusted 1Y expected return
(conviction.py; the options market's part at quarter Kelly, the research part scaled 0.5x-2x), and
Sigma_ij = rho_ij s_i s_j: s_i the s.d. of the name's final blended 1Y distribution (result.json, the same one that sets
target, TP and SL), rho_ij from the Risk Prism factor model recalibrated to the option market (riskcal.py), else 2Y
realized correlation shrunk toward the pool average. Constraints per name, the smallest binding:
  - Gate: no buy unless the NTM target (blended median) is above the last price ('target_above_last').
  - Stop budget: a stop-out at the SL may cost at most stop_budget_share_of_wealth of total wealth (data/review_settings.json;
    5% since Kilian 2026-09-29, was 2%): w <= budget / ((spot - SL) / spot).
  - The supervisor's sizing.max_weight_pct, if given, and a 20% single-name ceiling.
  - Index fund (review_settings index_fund, SPY since Kilian 2026-09-29): an S&P 500 fund is always a candidate, expected
    to earn the risk-free rate plus the measured 7.69% equity premium with its option-implied vol; no stop, supervisor or conviction caps, only
    its own max_weight. It soaks up cash the stock picks leave idle, sized against them in the same solve.
  - Kelly split (Kilian 2026-09-29): the options-implied part of each expected return is sized at market_kelly_fraction
    (half Kelly), the research part at quarter Kelly; done by solving with mu_solve = rf + MKF*gamma*(m - rf) + alpha.
    Reported expected returns are the true mu, not mu_solve.
  - Conviction: no buy unless the supervisor's sizing.conviction is at least min_supervisor_conviction
    (data/review_settings.json; 'medium' from Kilian 2026-09-29; null = off since Kilian 2026-10-21 'get rid of the
    rubric', so only the Sharpe tests gate buys). While it is set, a name with no rating gets no buy.
  - Big-miss block (Kilian 2026-10-19 card 'Add flag'): no buy, and a staged new name's buy pauses, for 6 months after a
    big earnings miss (earnings_miss.py -> data/earnings_miss.json; gate 'big_miss_block').
  - Held names (Kilian 2026-10-19 15:21Z, SIZING = 'max_sharpe'): review.py sizes them to Sharpe-optimal (tangency)
    targets on mu_eff, scaled to the total this rule would hold; here they stay fixed and a new name must still raise
    the book's Sharpe (Sharpe test below).
Across the book: total buys <= cash. An optional industry limit (max_industry_risk_share; null = off, Kilian removed
the 40% limit 2026-09-29) caps any one Risk Prism industry's share of the book's variance. Held names (holdings mode) stay fixed at
their current weight; review.py decides trims and adds for those. Whole shares: rounded down, then single shares added
back while they raise the objective and fit the cash and limits. The rest stays in cash.
runs/DATE/portfolio.json carries the book's expected return, volatility (recalibrated model, plus the raw model and the
option market's own view), Sharpe, beta, factor and industry risk shares.
portfolio.calibration_method:
The raw weekly model (../risk/riskcalc.py) runs below what stocks actually do: on 2026-09-28 its single-name vols sat
under both 1Y implied and realized vol (SPCX 27% vs 53% implied, EL 29% vs 42%, META 32% vs 42%), and its S&P 500 factor
vol was 14.1% vs 16.0% implied. Most of the shortfall is stock-specific risk; the factors run a little low too.
Two fixes, the same idea as Barra's volatility regime adjustment:
  1. Factor scale: multiply the whole factor covariance by k^2 so the model's S&P 500 vol equals the market's implied vol
     (SPY 30D full-strike IV from ../portfolio/data/iv, else the latest VIX).
  2. Specific top-up: set each name's specific variance so its total vol equals its 1Y implied vol from the option chain
     (priors/DATE/SYM.json atm_iv_1y; else 1Y realized): s_i^2 = max(target_i^2 - k^2 * factor_var_i, (0.05)^2).
Factor exposures and factor correlations are untouched, so names still co-move through the same factors, but a name whose
extra risk is its own (a new listing, a deal, earnings) no longer looks more correlated than it is.
Usage: import riskcal; M = riskcal.load(DATE)  -> riskcalc.Model with .calib (k, targets, raw vols) attached.

tax_assumptions._ignore_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: ignore taxes for now (he has money set aside for the liability). Set false to use the tax facts below.
tax_assumptions._future_note: Combined rate you'd expect on today's embedded gains when you'd otherwise sell (15% federal + ~6% state once working). Drives the sell cost and the gain-harvest suggestion.
tax_assumptions._tax_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: taxable account; ~$20,000 internship wages in 2026 plus realized gains; claimed as a dependent by a parent living in CA; full-time student under 24 living in CT. Assumed (not confirmed): domicile stays CA (a student living away at school keeps the parents' domicile, FTB Pub 1031), CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode so CT does not tax investment income; kiddie tax applies (earned income not more than half of his support). Federal 2026 figures from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32; CA brackets are 2025 (FTB Tax News Oct 2025), 2026's not published yet.
tax_assumptions._other_unearned_note: Dividends etc. this year (rough: GOOGL + META dividends). Counts toward the kiddie-tax threshold.
tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.
tax_assumptions._parent_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: parent in NYC, 37% federal bracket. Parent's NY/NYC rates do not apply to Kilian's gains (no NY kiddie tax under Form 8615).
tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

CNH Q2 2026 (Aug 3): management says this is the trough (dealer inventory normalised, fleets ageing) but sees no evidence yet of a sustained recovery. NA tractors -16/-17% in Q2. 2026 EPS guide is $0.41-0.46, so estimates are not yet rising. Deere is already +46% off its low. Too early to pick: no estimate support.

industrials.theme: Residential HVAC, pool and housing weakness
industrials.evidence: RRX's PES segment fell 6.6% organically on residential HVAC and pool (Aug 5). Generac residential sales -2% in Q2. This is a known drag and is in the price of mixed names.

tech.theme: Hyperscaler AI capex still rising into 2027
tech.evidence: A July 2026 report has the largest cloud operators' combined 2026 capex up ~89% y/y to ~$710B (prior +72%); BofA (Arya) sees global cloud/AI infrastructure capex approaching $1.5T by 2027; TSMC lifted 2026 capex to $60-64B (Jul 2026). The GPU/custom-silicon leaders already price this in (MRVL at ~65x FY1/38x FY2 EPS, +287% off its 52w low; CIEN ~38x FY27). Sources: finance.yahoo.com semis $1.3T article (2026); news.ainauten.com chip-capex-doubt story (Jul 2026).

tech.theme: Value migrating to rack-scale integration and data-center power (EMS/ODM)
tech.evidence: Flex's Cloud and Power Infrastructure unit is guided to grow 65-75% in FY27 (Jul 29, 2026 call) and Flex sold $2.0B of preferred in it (Axiom) at a $37.5B EV on 2026-10-05, vs Flex's own EV of ~$46.6B. Sanmina's ZT Systems (bought from AMD Oct 2025) runs at a $5-6B annual rate, and management says FY27 revenue will exceed $16B. Both stocks sit 25-30% below their June 2026 highs even though guidance went up, so the market has not yet repriced them for this growth.

tech.theme: Advanced packaging, HBM and silicon photonics/optical interconnect
tech.evidence: Onto raised its 2026 advanced-packaging growth outlook to ~80% from 50%, has a >$1B backlog and won a >$200M Dragonfly order from one OSAT for 2027 delivery (Aug 6, 2026). Amkor expects advanced-packaging revenue to triple in 2026. GlobalFoundries' photonics-led data-center segment grew 62% y/y and is targeted to double in 2026, with a $1B run-rate exiting 2028. Semtech guides Q3 FY27 revenue +20% q/q on data-center ACC/LPO.

Gartner projects 2026 DRAM/NAND prices +125%/+234%, with relief not until late 2027. UBS sees DRAM undersupplied until at least 2Q28 (streetinsider, 2026). SNDK is +1183% on 12-1 momentum and WDC/MU have already re-rated. The second-order effect is negative for phone and PC demand: GFS guides its mobile segment down low-teens in 2026 and Qualcomm's China OEM demand is weak.

tech.theme: Semis volatility: AI-capex durability doubts and China equipment
tech.evidence: In late July 2026 the SOX fell into a bear market on AI-spend durability doubts and reports of Chinese state-backed tool production. KLAC fell >6% despite a beat (Jul 28-29, 2026; quiverquant, sentisense), GFS fell 34% from Jun 22 to Jul 21 (tickeron) and ONTO fell ~44% from its June high to its July low. Estimates kept rising through that selloff, which is where today's entry points come from.

tech.theme: Software: AI-agent seat-compression scare, then rebound to usage-priced names
tech.evidence: IGV fell ~30% in early 2026 on the 'SaaSpocalypse' (seat-based pricing fears), then rose ~42% from its April low by Jun 3 (Reuters via finance.yahoo.com, 2026-06-03). Security, observability and communications names have since run hard (OKTA +264%, CRWD +189%, TWLO +148%, NET +117% over 6 months) and now mostly trade above their average analyst targets, so I took no software picks. Prices and monthly history come from Twelve Data quote/time_series. WebSearch worked throughout.

ideas.summary: Materials research is paused this week, so only the industrials and tech scouts were ranked. The themes were 2027 data-center power and rack-integration backlogs being valued at compressed multiples (GNRC, RRX, FLEX, SANM), a de-rated fiber/BEAD build (DY), the LTL freight inflection (SAIA) and AI packaging/photonics (ONTO, GFS, SMTC). The picks for a screen are GNRC (industrials, 26): consensus 2027 EPS +34% and revenue +32%, estimates up sharply since Q2 while the stock sits 24% below its high at ~17x 2027. FLEX (tech, 25) has a third-party $37.5B Axiom mark, EPS +43%/+50%, and spin and investor-day catalysts within six months. Both lean on data-center power, so they overlap VST and each other. DY (25, the cheapest at ~13x FY28) was the close alternative but lost on the one-per-sector rule, and SARO passed the defense check (military 17.8% of revenue) but has slower growth.

ideas.name: Generac Holdings Inc.
ideas.thesis: Data-center generators turn Generac from a residential-standby cyclical into a growth story: about $1.35B of its ~$1.6B data-center backlog ships in 2027, against about $450M of data-center revenue in 2026. A second hyperscale agreement, which management expects to be at least as large as the first, is not yet in backlog. Consensus now has revenue +32% and EPS +34% in 2027, yet the stock trades at ~17x 2027 EPS.
ideas.why_now: Q2 2026 (Jul 29): sales +11%, about $1B of new data-center orders in ~90 days, and the C&I and margin guides were raised. Estimates have moved up a lot since then: FY26 EPS went from ~$8.43 before Q2 to $9.69, and FY27 from ~$10.11 to $12.97. The stock is 24% below its high at $224.6, so the multiple has compressed while the numbers rose.

tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

memo.one_liner: Q3 held the earnings line: adj. EPS $1.42 and the FY2026 $5.50-5.55 midpoint reaffirmed. It cut the growth line: comparable growth ~6.0%, diabetes low-to-mid single digit, and a Nutrition spin by end-2027. At 17.0x a below-consensus ~$6.43 NTM EPS, net of ~$2.7B of litigation and separation cash, ABT is worth $107.79 (+9.6% vs the $98.36 post-print quote, derived: 107.79 / 98.36 - 1), so we keep the 16 sh @ $102.80 and stage the second tranche, which tonight's post-print re-mark sizes (+18 sh on the pre-print plan).

thesis.point: The print cut growth, not earnings, and our EPS already sits below the street.
thesis.evidence: Q3 adj. EPS $1.42 (+9.2%) on $13,013M sales (+7.0% comparable). The FY2026 adj. EPS midpoint was reaffirmed and the range narrowed to $5.50-5.55, and Q4 is guided to $1.62-1.67. The comparable-growth guide fell to ~6.0% (prior memo: 6.5-7.5%). Our horizon NTM adj. EPS of ~$6.43 (supervisor build) comes from that guide: FY2027 ~$6.06 and FY2028 ~$6.52, 0.3% and 3.2% under the pre-print Zacks consensus of $6.08 / $6.74 (supervisor figures on unrounded EPS; derived on the rounded figures: 6.06 / 6.08 - 1 = -0.3%, 6.52 / 6.74 - 1 = -3.3%), and 2.7% under a horizon-NTM consensus of ~$6.61 (derived: ~0.2 x $6.08 + ~0.8 x $6.74 = $6.61; 6.43 / 6.61 - 1 = -2.7%). Street cuts after the guide change should mostly converge toward our numbers, not below them.

thesis.point: The valuation needs no re-rating. We price 17.0x, which keeps a ~7% discount to peers and is only ~3% above today's multiple (derived: 17.0 / 18.2 - 1 = -6.6%; 17.0 / 16.5 - 1 = +3.0%).
thesis.evidence: On one calendar NTM window (2026-10-21 to 2027-10-20), ABT trades at 16.5x against an 18.2x median for 11 peers (supervisor rebase, derived: ABT $98.36 / (0.197 x $5.53 + 0.803 x $6.08 = $5.97) = 16.5x). The P/E leg uses 17.0x and the EV/EBITDA leg 13.3x, which is ABT's own multiple today (derived: EV ~$198.6B / ~$14.88B NTM adj. EBITDA in the build = 13.35x). The discount persists through the horizon for three reasons: Nutrition plus EPD are ~22% of FY2027 segment operating earnings in the reconciled build (derived: (1,621 + 1,481) / 14,277 = 21.7%; FY2025 10-K actual (1,558 + 1,290) / 11,800 = 24.1%) at staples/generics multiples until a spin that most likely lands after 2027-10-20, CGM growth is slower and Medicare bidding pricing starts ~2028, and ~12,700 NEC infants are still pending. The 17.0x / 13.3x multiple was chosen on the 2026-10-21 decision card over the 18.2x / 14.0x peer median, which would give $115.00 (supervisor).

thesis.point: The known liabilities are now sized and deducted. The Nutrition separation is value-neutral, and any re-rating it brings is upside we do not count.
thesis.evidence: The research target (12m) deducts ~$2.67B after tax (derived: 520 + 350 + 750 + 150 + 600 + 300 = $2,670M): the ~$670M NEC deal (-$520M), the $384.2M DOJ/states settlement (-$350M), the ~12,700 remaining NEC infants (-$750M, supervisor estimate; derived: ~$970M pre-tax / ~12,700 = ~$76k per infant, ~2x the August deal's ~$35k = (~$670M - ~$600M Gill) / ~2,000), Libre 3 recall claims (-$300M x 0.5), specified-items cash (-$600M) and separation costs (-$300M). The 8-K describes a distribution of a ~$8.5B-sales Nutrition company, intended to qualify as tax-free, completion expected by end-2027, with a combined dividend equal to Abbott's. We carry a 10% chance that it distributes before 2027-10-20, which moves only the quote (~$9 lower on a distribution of equal value; derived by the supervisor as the mean of two agent estimates, ($10.7 + $7.35) / 2 = ~$9.0).

memo.variant_view: The variant view is small, and it points the other way from the street. Our $110.95 target and $107.79 research target (12m) sit well below the sell-side: mean $120.72, median $120, 28 analysts, Strong Buy, as of 2026-10-16 before the print, given zero weight. We think the street is stale. Pre-print FY2027/FY2028 consensus of $6.08 / $6.74 predates the cut to ~6.0% comparable growth, diabetes at low-to-mid single digit 'for the next few quarters', and EP guided to ~20% in Q4, and our build is already 0.3% / 3.2% below it. Against the options market we are only slightly more constructive: the market-only distribution has a $107.35 median and P(gain) 0.5633, against the published $110.95 and 0.6116. The research leg alone gives $110.78 / 0.6191. The supervisor's reconciled value ($107.79) sits on the five forecasters' mean ($107.67), and the supervisor claims no directional edge. Read this as a fairly priced, defensive compounder bought slightly below value, not a mispricing the market is missing. (Sources 1, 3, 9, 23, 24, 25.)

valuation.methods: The research target (12m) is $107.79, the model engine's base horizon value (2027-10-20) on the supervisor's reconciled inputs. It weights 0.6 x P/E (17.0x NTM adj. EPS of ~$6.43) and 0.4 x EV/EBITDA (13.3x NTM adj. EBITDA); both legs come to $107.79. It is net of ~$2.67B after-tax litigation, settlement, separation and specified-items cash, on 2026-06-30 net debt of $27,005M (derived: 3,005 + 29,603 - 5,104 - 499, 10-Q). Scenarios: bear $78.79 / base $107.79 / bull $132.55. The five agents' research targets (12m) run $104.53-$110.82 (median $107.96; mean $107.67, derived: (110.82 + 108.80 + 104.53 + 107.96 + 106.26) / 5). The multiple decision card gave three values: 17.0x / 13.3x at $107.79 (chosen), the 18.2x / 14.0x peer median at $115.00 ($114.92 before the citation-gate fixes), and today's 16.5x / 13.0x at $104.75. There is no DCF leg this round; the prior memo blended 0.4 DCF. The $110.95 target is the median of the published 12-month distribution, which weights the options market 0.67 and research 0.33 with a calibration shift (expected value $115.03). It is not the research target (12m). Upside from the $102.45 pre-print close is +8.30% to target and +5.21% to the research target (12m) (derived: 110.95 / 102.45 - 1; 107.79 / 102.45 - 1). From the $98.36 post-print quote it is +12.8% and +9.6% (derived: 110.95 / 98.36 - 1; 107.79 / 98.36 - 1). Changes vs the 2026-10-14 memo: target $110.01 to $110.95 (+$0.94), research target (12m) $114.08 to $107.79 (derived: -$6.29, -5.5%), TP $130.57 to $133.60, stop $82.51 to $82.70, thesis break $80 to $78. The research target (12m) fell on 17.5x to 17.0x, dropping the DCF leg, slower Libre and EP after the call, and a fuller litigation/separation deduction. All levels are from the pre-print 2026-10-20 close and are re-marked tonight on the post-print close. (Sources 6, 7, 11, 24, 25, 30, 31, 36.)

The January 2027 guide. FY2027 adj. EPS at or above ~$6.0 with organic growth accelerating from ~6% confirms the build, and we build toward 34 sh. A guide well below $6.0, or diabetes still decelerating in Q4, breaks the earnings leg of the thesis, and we cut and re-run.

Litigation and Libre quality. An NEC settlement batch above ~2x our ~$76k per infant, or a Libre consent decree or second recall, means our deductions are too small and we cut. A CMS non-insulin type 2 coverage decision or a warning-letter close-out is upside not in the numbers, and we would add on weakness.

memo.title: AMAT: staged Long after a 17.6% sell-off with no AMAT 8-K left it 14.6% below its $523 research target (12m)
memo.call_reason: The published 12-month target of $494.60 is 10.7% above the $446.63 close, conviction is medium and the Sharpe gate passed, so the book takes 5 shares, staged around the October prints and FQ4.
memo.one_liner: AMAT fell from $542.28 (Oct 5) to $446.63 (Oct 14) with no AMAT 8-K filing; since Sept 29 Micron, ASML and TSMC have all printed strong, and SEMI's 2028 WFE forecast is now $220B, which supports the $23.85 FY28 consensus. We buy 5 shares in tranches for a $494.60 target (research target (12m) $523), with a $328.23 stop just under the $335 thesis break.

thesis.point: The equipment upcycle runs through 2028, and it is being raised, not cut.
thesis.evidence: SEMI has WFE +21.8% in 2027 and raised its 2028 forecast to $220B from ~$200B on Sept 1, which supports consensus FY28 EPS of $23.85 on $55.9B of sales. Since our Sept 29 research, Micron printed record FQ4 revenue of $54.23B and guided FQ1 FY27 to $61.5B +/- $1.5B. ASML guided Q4 to EUR 14.2-15.2B and says planned 2027-28 supply will not fully meet customer demand. TSMC guided Q4 revenue to US$52.3-54.3B.

thesis.point: The market has already done much of the de-rating our research target (12m) assumes.
thesis.evidence: The close fell from $512.01 on Sept 29 to $446.63 on Oct 14, including -6.7% on Oct 13 (from $497.53) and -3.8% on Oct 14. AMAT filed no 8-K between Aug 27 and Oct 15. At $446.63 the stock is ~24.2x FY27 consensus EPS of $18.43, against ~27.8x at research ($512.01; derived). The research target (12m), derived, is NTM EPS of ~$22.8 (FY28 consensus less 4.5%) x 22.5x + $10.03 net cash = ~$522.5, rounded to $523, so the gap to the research target (12m) has widened from ~2% to 17.1%.

thesis.point: The next two quarters of earnings are visible, and the balance sheet is net cash.
thesis.evidence: The Q4 FY26 guide is revenue of $10.25B +/- $0.5B and non-GAAP EPS of $4.02 +/- $0.20. FY26 sales come to ~$34.3B (derived: 9M $24.04B + the $10.25B guide midpoint), and FY27 consensus is $46.3B (+35%, derived). Net cash is $7,957M ($10.03/share; derived from the 10-Q balance sheet). FQ3 converted 83% of non-GAAP net income to FCF (derived: $2,330M / $2,795M), against 51% over 9M (derived: $5,568M operating cash flow less $1,988M capex = $3,580M, over $6,980M), so the AR build reversing would add cash.

We are well below it: the StockAnalysis median target is $645.50 (40 analysts, Strong Buy, range $358-900) [10], and our recency-weighted median of the individual targets is $654.18 (result.json), while our $494.60 target and $523 research target (12m) assume the multiple compresses to ~22.5x NTM as the cycle ages. tax_assumptions._ignore_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: ignore taxes for now (he has money set aside for the liability). Set false to use the tax facts below.
tax_assumptions._future_note: Combined rate you'd expect on today's embedded gains when you'd otherwise sell (15% federal + ~6% state once working). Drives the sell cost and the gain-harvest suggestion.
tax_assumptions._tax_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: taxable account; ~$20,000 internship wages in 2026 plus realized gains; claimed as a dependent by a parent living in CA; full-time student under 24 living in CT. Assumed (not confirmed): domicile stays CA (a student living away at school keeps the parents' domicile, FTB Pub 1031), CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode so CT does not tax investment income; kiddie tax applies (earned income not more than half of his support). Federal 2026 figures from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32; CA brackets are 2025 (FTB Tax News Oct 2025), 2026's not published yet.
tax_assumptions._other_unearned_note: Dividends etc. this year (rough: GOOGL + META dividends). Counts toward the kiddie-tax threshold.
tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.
tax_assumptions._parent_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: parent in NYC, 37% federal bracket. Parent's NY/NYC rates do not apply to Kilian's gains (no NY kiddie tax under Form 8615).
tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

agents.reasoning: Delta refresh of my 2026-09-29 view ($263 FV, P(>=247) 0.59). What changed in the evidence: (1) No new 8-K/10-Q since Sep 29; EDGAR shows only a Form 4 (a $251.5k 10b5-1 sale by Herrington). The pre-Sep-29 filings I had missed are the GBP 4.25B notes (FWP Sep 9, closed Sep 14 per 8-K, listed on Nasdaq per 8-A12B Sep 24) and a new director (Mandia, 8-K 5.02). The notes raise gross debt and confirm continued debt funding of capex, but are net-neutral at issue. (2) The stock rose 3.9% (246.67 to 256.33) vs QQQ +2.9%, MSFT +4.0%, GOOGL +2.0%, ORCL +5.1%, META flat. That is mostly beta to a Nasdaq at record highs after weak payrolls cut October hike odds to ~20% (Polymarket, $26.9M). There was no company-specific news: the press center shows only AWS customer releases, and the TD Cowen Buy reiteration was a non-event. (3) Consensus edged up: FY26 normalized $8.15 to $8.31, FY27 $10.48 to $10.51 (Yahoo, 4 up / 0 down in 30 days), and I now have a sourced FY28 consensus of $13.81 (MarketScreener), where last week I used my own +20% ($12.56). (4) The new peer-set rule: 11 comps on one FY~CY2027 basis (median 26.7x P/E, 13.5x EV/EBITDA). (5) Method fixes: the SOTP is now rolled to horizon NTM earnings, consistent with the P/E leg; last week it applied today's forward multiples to 2027 earnings, which is a value as of today rather than at the horizon. Net debt now uses the consensus path to Oct-2027 (~$61B) instead of a Q2 proxy (~$31B), and the retail multiple rose from 20x to 22x to stay defensibly inside the peer range. Result: P/E $282 to $298 (FY28 input $12.56 to $13.40, multiple 23.5x unchanged), SOTP $244 to $282, FV $263 to $290. I do not move the forecast distribution all the way to the FV: most of the +$27 is inputs and method, not news, and FV estimates are noisy, so the ladder uses a three-component lognormal mixture (medians 198/280/355, weights 25/50/25, sigmas 0.30/0.19/0.24). That gives a median of ~$278 (+8.5%), mean ~$286, and log-sd ~0.31, close to the 34% realized vol (slightly below, since the dispersion of scenario medians already adds spread). P(>=256) is 0.618 and P(>=449) 0.045. Source mix: the 11 required comp pages and consensus pages push the in-lane share to 12/32 (~38%). Among non-comp sources it is 12/21 (~57%), below the 60% target because the comp rule requires a data page per peer. Lane-unique items: the GBP notes FWP/8-K/8-A12B, the Item 5.02 8-K, the Form 4 and the 10-Q note detail. Not used (unverified): CNN on Anthropic IPO timing (HTTP 451), payroll figures (secondary only), and Microsoft/Alphabet report dates beyond Trefis's estimate.

agents.reasoning: Lane: skeptic. I read the 10-Q, the 10-K and six 2026 debt documents first. Amazon has gone from $65.6B of long-term debt (Dec-25) to ~$164B face by Sept-26, through USD, EUR, CHF, CAD and GBP issues with coupons up to 6.65% and maturities to 2076. It also signed a $17.5B delayed-draw term loan. TTM FCF is -$7.6B, $29.3B of capex was accrued but not yet paid, and Moody's cut the outlook to stable (external funding). The bigger red flag is circularity: Amazon put $50B into OpenAI and $10B into Anthropic in H1-26, and both labs made $100B+ AWS commitments. Meanwhile $62.8B of H1 pre-tax income came from Level 3 Anthropic mark-ups - so GAAP 2026 EPS ($12.88 consensus) overstates operating earnings; I value only the 2027-28 operating EPS and add the stakes at a 50% haircut. Fitzgerald calls the OpenAI framework 'circular financing'. Amazon also has a precedent of over-building, with the 2021-22 fulfillment glut (shareholder-suit record). Weighed honestly, though: the accounting critique (Burry) mostly spares Amazon, which shortened server lives to 5 years in 2025. Insider activity is routine RSU sales plus Bezos gifts, with no cluster selling. AWS re-accelerated to 37% with $496B of backlog, which rebuts DA Davidson's Feb 'losing the lead' downgrade. Credit is A1/AA with no covenants. So the skeptic case is about FCF quality and valuation, not solvency or fraud. On 12 peers (one MarketScreener basis, FY ending Jun-27 to May-28), AMZN is near the median P/E and below the median EV/EBITDA. Applying below-median multiples and a capex-file-based EPS haircut gives ~$296-300 for the multiple methods. A DCF at a market-implied 10.4% WACC gives only $144, which shows how much of the price rests on long-run margins and low discount rates. Blended fair value is $267 (+4%). Scenarios are $195/$265/$340 at 25/50/25, for an expected ~$266. The ladder blends that scenario mixture with a lognormal (median $262, sigma 0.34, close to the 34% realized vol), so P(>=$256) = 0.54. It is slightly less bullish than the multiple methods alone and well below the $330.59 street target, which I treat as evidence but not the answer. No option data was used.

memo.title: AMZN: Long. Hold 1 sh into the Oct 29 print and add toward ~11 sh after it. Target $280.84 (+12.2%), research target (12m) $278.28 on 23x driver-built EPS plus an AWS-led sum of parts
memo.call_reason: The published target ($280.84) and research target (12m) ($278.28) are both above the $250.38 close, and P(gain) is 0.6279. The edge is modest: the supervisor's confidence is low (its ladder is not used), and conviction scales the expected return from 18.3% to 17.5% (multiplier 0.72).
memo.one_liner: AWS is adding capacity faster than ever: AWS net PP&E reached $263.8B at mid-2026 against a ~$496B backlog. Our driver build turns that into AWS sales of $234.6B in 2027 (+35%) and lets ads carry retail profits. The Anthropic and OpenAI stakes add ~$21/share, which the street's EPS does not count. We price 23x on NTM EPS of $11.32, 13% below consensus; the gap is EBITDA, not D&A (2028: $297.9B vs consensus $355.3B), so the $278.28 research target (12m) and $280.84 target are not stretch numbers; we hold 1 sh and stage the add after the Oct 29 print.

thesis.point: AWS growth is capacity-led and largely pre-sold, so revenue follows the capex.
thesis.evidence: Q2-26 AWS sales were $42.2B (+37%) with $16.6B OI. The backlog is ~$496B with a 6.4-year weighted life, and management says power capacity doubles by end-2027 vs 2025 and 2027 capacity is largely reserved. The driver build rolls AWS net PP&E from $150.4B (FY25 average) to $266.2B / $426.3B / $590.8B averages in 2026-28. Capacity turnover falls from 0.86x to 0.65x / 0.55x / 0.50x. That gives AWS sales of $173.8B / $234.6B / $293.7B, which is +35.0% in 2027 and +25.2% in 2028 (derived: 234.6 / 173.8 - 1; 293.7 / 234.6 - 1). AWS EBITDA margin goes from 57.1% in H1-26 (ex the ~$0.6B energy gain) to 58.5% / 60.0%. The external backdrop is supportive: the cloud market grew +43% y/y in Q2 with Amazon at 28% share, and AWS raised Capacity Block GPU prices ~15% on Oct 7 (P6-B300 now $16.146 per accelerator-hour; the prior $14.04 is from the research).

thesis.point: Ads, not the stores, carry North America + International profit, and that profit compounds even with flat retail margins.
thesis.evidence: Advertising was $68.6B in FY25 and grew +25.1% in H1-26 (Q2 +26.2%). The driver path is $85.4B / $102.5B / $121.0B for 2026-28 (+24% / +20% / +18%). At an assumed 50% ads margin, which is our estimate and not disclosed, stores run at ~0.16% margin held flat. Segment OI still rises from $43.7B in 2026 to $52.3B in 2027 and $61.6B in 2028 (engine rows). The SOTP values this at 22x NTM after-tax OI of $46.9B = $1,032B.

thesis.point: The AI-lab stakes are real equity value that consensus EPS excludes. We count them once, after tax, lock-up and an overlay.
thesis.evidence: The 10-Q carries Anthropic at $190.4B, and Amazon committed $50B to OpenAI's Series C. We value Anthropic at a $1.5T IPO, which is 17.60% after the Public Benefit Fund and primary dilution, less 24% tax and a 10.37% lock-up discount, for $183.7B. OpenAI is at cost, $50.0B. Together that is ~$21.19/share on 11.03B horizon shares (derived: (183.7 + 50.0) / 11.03). After the Leo and Zoox loss add-backs (+$72.7B) and their own scenario values (+$22.0B), other investments (+$4.6B), Globalstar (-$10.9B), probability-weighted legal (-$34.5B) and a 10% conglomerate overlay (-$26.0B), the net equity-level items are +$23.72/share (derived: $261.6B / 11.03B) on both legs. The stakes cut both ways: an Anthropic IPO at ~$1.0T takes ~$6.95/share off, and ~$1.92T adds ~$5.53.

memo.variant_view: We sit below the street and slightly above the options market. StockAnalysis shows a median target of $329.50 (average $331.46, Strong Buy); our recency-weighted median of 56 individual analyst targets is $326.23, +30.3% from $250.38. Our $280.84 target is 13.9% below it (derived: 280.84 / 326.23 - 1), and analysts get zero weight in the published target (ex-analyst target $276.13). The gap is earnings, not the multiple. Our driver-built NTM EPS at the Oct-2027 horizon is $11.32, against ~$13.03 on consensus (derived: 0.237 x $10.51 + 0.763 x $13.81), so we are 13.1% below. Driver-built 2028 EBIT is $155.1B vs MarketScreener's $182.7B (-15.1%). The difference is not D&A. We depreciate AWS PP&E at 14% a year on a capex roll that uses consensus 2027-28 capex ($277.4B / $296.9B), yet the build's 2028 D&A of $142.7B is below the $172.6B implied by consensus EBITDA less EBIT (derived: 355.3 - 182.7). The gap is EBITDA: $297.9B vs $355.3B in 2028 (-16.2%, derived), with the stores margin held at ~0.16% (H1-26 0.76%) and ads at an assumed 50% margin. The street's ~$326 implies ~31x FY27 EPS (derived: 326.23 / 10.51 = 31.0x), against a 23.5x CY2027 peer median. Against the options market, the market-only median is $265.01 with P(gain) 0.5615. Our published $280.84 is 6.0% higher (derived: 280.84 / 265.01 - 1) and our P(gain) of 0.6279 is 6.6 points higher. The gap comes from the research leg (weight 0.33, with its calibration shift), whose value includes the ~$21/share of AI-lab stakes. This is a real but small variant: a below-consensus earnings path, with sum-of-parts value the street's P/E does not capture.

valuation.methods: The research target (12m) of $278.28 is the model engine's base horizon value (2027-10-06) on the driver-led set: 0.5 x P/E leg + 0.5 x SOTP leg. P/E leg $284.09: 23x (a 2.3% discount to the 23.5x CY2027 11-peer median; cloud subgroup 22.5x) x driver-built NTM EPS $11.32 = $260.36, plus $23.72/share of equity-level items. SOTP leg $272.47: AWS NTM after-tax OI $70.9B x 25 = $1,772.5B, plus North America + International $46.9B x 22 = $1,032.0B, less a $3.2B venture basis correction = EV $2,801.4B. From that we deduct horizon net debt of $58.4B (incl. finance leases) and add the same equity items, over 11.03B horizon shares (0.9%/yr dilution). The DCF is a diagnostic only, at weight 0 ($182 at a 10.44% WACC with a mid-capex-cycle terminal year). Scenarios are bear $183.10 (p 0.25: AWS turnover -8%, EBITDA margin -2 pts, ads -4%, 17.5x, Anthropic ~$1.0T), base $278.28 (p 0.5) and bull $343.83 (p 0.25: AWS turnover +6%, +1.5 pts, ads +3%, 25.5x, Anthropic ~$1.92T). The model median is $270.60. The driver gate (2026-10-22) moved the research target (12m) $277.36 -> $278.28 by fixing the EPS/EBIT ratio. The three agents' research targets (12m) were $290 / $278 / $267. The $280.84 target is the median of the published 12-month distribution, which weights the options market 0.67 and research 0.33 with a calibration shift (expected value $296.27). Upside from $250.38 is +12.17% to target and +11.14% to the research target (12m) (derived: 280.84 / 250.38 - 1; 278.28 / 250.38 - 1).

agents.reasoning: Round 2. Primary documents still show a fast-compounding business: Q2 2026 revenue $1.924B (+53%), 83.9% adj. EBITDA margin, $3.76 GAAP EPS, Q3 guide $2.055-2.085B (+46-48%), net debt ~$0.46B, $1.8B buyback authorisation left. Corrections from the supervisor, which I verified: (1) the Q3 guide is not conservative in the way I said; the CFO said it 'reflects the model improvements that are already live and performing' (the step-up that landed just after quarter-end) and excludes only not-yet-deployed releases; (2) Edgewater's Q4 call (+8-9% q/q) is only ~1-2% below consensus; (3) Wells Fargo's traffic-weighted pixel data pushes e-commerce to 2027. Re-reading the call I also found I overstated the buyback pace: Q2 repurchases were $551M, moderated from ~$1B in Q1. I therefore cut FY27 EPS 4% to $19.2, FY28 growth to 18%, the P/E to 16x and the share-count reduction, which lowers fair value from $382 to $348 (P/E $349, FCF yield $348). I remain above the supervisor's ~$320 because 15x NTM is roughly today's de-rated multiple and assumes no re-rating at all for a business still guiding ~46% growth; a modest move to 16x is a judgment I keep. The scenario mix (30% bear $175, 45% base $320, 25% bull $490) gives a mean of ~$319. I do not centre the distribution on fair value because revisions are falling and momentum is negative. The ladder is a mixture: 92% lognormal with median $308 and sigma 0.55, plus 8% business-break mass with median $155. That gives P(>=281) 0.53, slightly below round 1's 0.545, and a thinner right tail (P>=703 0.062 vs 0.071). EDGAR shows no new 8-K since Aug 5. Research was mostly SEC filings and the call transcript; consensus is from Alpha Vantage, and option data was deliberately not consulted.

The supervisor showed (a) Edgewater's Q4 call is only ~1-2% below consensus revenue, so my 5% EPS cut plus a further 5% EBITDA trim double-counted it; (b) the Citi/Store Leads raw merchant counts I used as an offset are inflated by dormant APAC storefronts: Wells Fargo's traffic-weighted data (which I verified: 85% zero-traffic new sites vs ~30% pre-June, e-commerce 'more like a 2027 story', EW $325 PT) is the better read. I now use one consistent ~3-3.5% trim to FY27 revenue/EPS across all legs and drop the Citi offset. New lane evidence: AppLovin sued Unity (Sep 27-Oct 1) to stop its Ad Quality SDK collecting MAX auction data, with a TRO hearing and a JAMS arbitration; Unity calls it an incumbent's response to 'increased competition and slowing growth'. I read that as confirming that Unity Vector (Q3 Strategic Grow guided +68-70%, Vector >$1B run rate) is a real competitive threat, which justifies trimming the P/E to 15.5x from 16x, though a win would protect MAX's data edge. Sensor Tower still has APP at ~36% of game ad revenue (AdMob 29%) in a game-ad pool growing ~8%, so gaming growth must come from share or pricing. Net: P/E leg $352->$344, EV/EBITDA $309->$320 (double haircut removed, multiple aligned with P/E), FCF $330->$333; blend ~$333, basically unchanged because removing the double count is offset by a lower multiple and the loss of the e-commerce offset. Scenarios 185/325/500 at 30/45/25 (mean ~$327). Ladder: lognormal, median ~$300, sigma 0.57 (below the 75% realized because ~14x EPS, ~6% FCF yield and buybacks give valuation support), with a 3% crash component (median $140) for litigation/fraud-type tails; P(>=281) 0.53. Supervisor facts outside my lane (SEC probe closed, CEO sales under 10b5-1) slightly reduce the governance tail, which is why the crash weight is small. 1-month: no AppLovin earnings in window (est. disagreements.topic: Size of the haircut to FY2027 consensus EPS ($20.00)
disagreements.resolution: Partly settled. Edgewater's specific call is Q4 revenue +8-9% q/q, i.e. ~$2.24-2.26B on a ~$2.07B Q3, only ~1-2% below the ~$2.27-2.28B consensus implies. That alone does not justify a 7-8% FY27 EPS cut. The Wells Fargo traffic-weighted pixel work (85% of new sites with no traffic; e-commerce 'more like a 2027 story') supports a modest further trim to the e-commerce ramp. A ~3-5% haircut is better supported than 0% or 8%.

disagreements.topic: Status of the SEC data-practices probe
disagreements.resolution: Closed. The CFO said on the Aug 5 2026 Q2 call that the SEC concluded its inquiry with no recommended action. The Q2 10-Q discloses no SEC or state-AG matter and accrues no material loss. agent_5 is wrong. Remaining legal risk is the 2025 class action (motion to dismiss pending) and the new Talbot class action (lead-plaintiff deadline Nov 16 2026).

Corrected. The CEO's March and June 2026 sales (e.g. $14.6m on Jun 10, $11.2m on Jun 12) were made under a Rule 10b5-1 plan adopted Mar 3 2026. One caveat is fair: the plan was adopted inside the Feb 12 - Aug 5 class period, so plaintiffs may still cite it. It is weaker evidence of scienter than agent_3 implied.

Wells Fargo's traffic-weighted measure is the better-quality read on revenue. The raw counts are inflated by dormant APAC Shopify storefronts: the zero-traffic share of new sites rose from ~30% before June to ~85% recently. The Jefferies survey covers only 30 advertisers. E-commerce is a 2027 option, not a 2026 driver; that supports a modest haircut but is not thesis-breaking.

The ladders differ little (max spread ~0.06 at mid strikes; agent_4 has a much thinner far-right tail, 0.014 at $703 vs 0.045-0.071 for the others). My searches gave no fact that clearly moves the centre, so I keep the mean ladder. Reconciled fair value is ~$320: agent_1's 0% haircut and 17x on a $23 NTM EPS is on the generous side, while the 8% haircuts double-count Edgewater.

memo.title: AppLovin: cheap at about 14x FY27 EPS but conviction is low. The model says no position; a 1-share post-print starter would be an exception to the conviction rule.
memo.call_reason: Conviction is below medium: the supervisor rated it low, so the allocator sized it at 0 shares (binding: conviction_below_min). The target of $292.84 is above the $268.22 price, so the target is not what blocks the trade; low conviction is.
memo.one_liner: APP trades at about 14x FY27 EPS with a 6% FCF yield, $0.46B net debt and $1.8B of buyback left. Our $292.84 target (+9%) and $322 research target (12m) (+20%) are well below the Street's $512 median, and the model takes no position because conviction is low. The only trade on the table is a proposal awaiting your yes: 1 share (about $268) after the Q3 print and Q4 guide, expected around Wed Nov 4 but not yet announced. It is an explicit exception to the medium-conviction rule, justified by its effect on the book's Sharpe, not by a stronger view on the stock.

thesis.point: The business is still growing fast and is very profitable. The de-rating comes from slower growth, not shrinking earnings.
thesis.evidence: Q2 2026 revenue was $1,924M (+53% y/y), adjusted EBITDA $1,614M (84% margin), diluted EPS $3.76 and free cash flow $863.3M. The Q3 2026 guide is revenue of $2,055-2,085M (about +7.6% q/q at the midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA of $1,710-1,740M (83% margin).

thesis.point: Valuation and the balance sheet give a floor. Further downside needs earnings estimates to fall, not just the multiple.
thesis.evidence: At $268 the stock is about 14x FY27 consensus EPS of $20.00 and about a 6% FCF yield (supervisor). At Jun 30 2026: cash $3,053M against long-term debt $3,515M, so net debt is about $0.46B. Shares outstanding were 335.3M. The company bought back 3.28M shares for $1.5B in H1 2026, and $1.8B of authorization remains. The thesis break of $185 equals about 9x FY27 EPS and a 10%+ FCF yield.

thesis.point: The upside needs the estimate cuts to stop, and the Q4 guide is the first chance for that. This is why we would enter after the print, not before.
thesis.evidence: FY27 consensus EPS fell from $21.16 to $20.00 in 60 days (19 cuts, 5 raises; vendor data). Edgewater expects Q4 at +8-9% q/q (about $2.25B), against a consensus of about $2.27-2.28B. Wells Fargo's traffic-weighted pixel data (about 85% of new sites show no traffic) suggests e-commerce is a 2027 story. A Q4 guide at or above consensus would stop the cuts. A guide below about $2.25B would extend them.

memo.variant_view: Our variant view is against the sell side, not against the options market. Our blended 12-month target is $292.84 (P(gain) 0.55). The 24 analysts' weighted mean is $511 (median $512, range $325-790, rating Buy). We think those targets are stale: they assume a re-rating that falling revisions do not support. In the last two months BofA moved to $400 and Piper to $325, and Wells Fargo is at $325. The options market alone implies $252 (P(gain) 0.46). We sit modestly above it because valuation support (14x, 6% FCF yield, buybacks) has not yet broken. That edge over the options market is small, about +$41 in the median, and at about 68% implied vol it is not a strong variant view. The supervisor said plainly that no verified fact shows a clear edge per unit of risk. [sources 20, 23, 24, 25, 18, 22]

valuation.methods: Supervisor research target (12m) $322, against the agents' range of $310-348 (mean $326). Three methods, blended: (1) P/E: FY27 EPS of about $19.2 (consensus $20.00 less about 4%), rolled to an NTM EPS of about $22 at Oct 2027, at about 15x = about $330. (2) FCF yield: FY27E FCF of about $6.4B / about 328M shares at a 6-6.3% yield = about $310-325. (3) EV/EBITDA: 11-12x on about $8.1B, less $0.46B net debt = about $290-320. Share base: 335.3M at Jun 30 2026 (10-Q), falling to about 326-330M with buybacks. The 12-month target ($292.84) is the calibrated median of a 67% options-market / 33% agent blend. Scenario range across agents: bear $170-190 (22-30%), base $310-325 (45-53%), bull $475-500 (25-27%). Model take-profit $453.69 (q75); stop $180.70 (2x 1M IV noise floor). [sources 2, 20, 22]

trade.position: Proposed: 1 sh (about $268 at the $268.22 close, about 2.7% of the $9,976 book). This is an explicit EXCEPTION to the medium-conviction rule. The model allocation is 0 shares because the supervisor rated conviction low (binding: conviction_below_min). The case for the exception is the portfolio effect: 1 APP share, alongside 1 AMZN share, raises the book's Sharpe on invested money from about 0.60 to about 0.68. 1 share is slightly above the supervisor's 2.5% cap (about $249), and a single share cannot be split into the supervisor's two tranches.
trade.entry: Do not buy before the print. Buy 1 share after the Q3 2026 report and Q4 guide (expected around Wed Nov 4 2026; the company has not announced the date as of Oct 3), and only if all three hold: (a) the Q4 revenue guide midpoint is at or above about $2.25B (Edgewater's bar); (b) the stock is above the $185 thesis break; (c) nothing new turns up in litigation or the Unity dispute. This adapts the supervisor's two-tranche plan (half after Q3, half after Q4 in Feb 2027) to a 1-share size. If the guide misses, there is no trade.
trade.exit_or_add: Exit if: the stock closes below the $180.70 stop or holds below the $185 thesis break (loss at stop about $88, about 0.9% of the book); the Q4 2026 report (around mid-Feb 2027) misses its own guide, or the Q1 2027 guide implies flat or negative q/q; FY27 consensus EPS falls below about $18; or AppLovin loses the Unity dispute in a way that exposes MAX auction data. Take profit at $453.69. Add a 2nd share only after the Q4 2026 report, if the guide held, FY27 revisions have stopped falling, and the supervisor's conviction rating rises to medium. Until then the position stays at 1 share as an exception.

what_changes_our_mind: Bullish: a Q4 guide at or above about $2.28B, with management quantifying e-commerce, and FY27 consensus EPS turning up from $20.00. This would justify medium conviction and a normal-sized position.
Bearish: a Q4 guide implying less than about +5% q/q, or a sustained trade below $185. Either would mean the market expects earnings to fall; we would drop the idea and not buy the exception share.

Competitive: Unity Q3 Strategic Grow beats $385M and guides Q4 to another mid-teens q/q while AppLovin decelerates, or the TRO is denied and Unity keeps collecting MAX auction data. Either would move weight to the bear case ($170-190).

memo.title: AVGO: long a de-rated AI compounder at ~13.5x FY28 consensus; target $390, research target (12m) $407, stop $261
memo.call_reason: The published 12-month target ($390.49) is above the $349.57 price, conviction is medium, and there is no special situation; the supervisor's 8% cap limits size and the book gets 2 shares.
memo.one_liner: Broadcom has fallen ~30% from its June high while earnings rose ~43%. It trades at ~13.5x LSEG FY28 EPS of $25.86, against management's $115B FY27 / $230B FY28 AI roadmap. We underwrite consensus EPS, not management's >$30, and still get a $407 research target (12m) (+16%) and a $390 target (+12%, P(gain) 60%), with the Q4 print on ~Dec 10 as the first test.

thesis.point: Earnings are compounding faster than the stock is falling: the de-rating is multiple, not fundamentals.
thesis.evidence: Q3 FY26 revenue $29.6B (+86% y/y), AI semis $16.7B (+221%), non-GAAP EPS $3.32, FCF $13.7B. The Q4 guide is $34.8B with $21.7B AI. Yet the stock is back at its end-2025 level with EPS ~43% higher and ~30% below the June high, at ~18x FY27 consensus ($19.38) and ~13.5x FY28 ($25.86).

thesis.point: We do not need management's numbers: consensus EPS at a below-peer multiple gets to ~$407.
thesis.evidence: Management guides $115B FY27 and $230B FY28 AI revenue and >$30 FY28 EPS; LSEG consensus is $25.86. All five agents value on NTM EPS of $24.7-26.5 at 16.5-17x, i.e. at or below consensus. Every $1 of FY28 EPS the market underwrites is worth ~$16-17/share, so each beat on the path toward >$30 is upside to the target.

thesis.point: The XPV financing scare is smaller than the headline: expected loss ~$0.5/share.
thesis.evidence: The 10-Q (Note 10) shows a Backstop of one customer's 5-year lease obligations: 85% of lease balance owed less rack resale value, max ~$29B, fair value not material, nothing paid, plus a facility under which the customer may issue Broadcom up to $42B of convertible notes (none issued). BofA's $370B is a hypothetical 20 GW build-out; its loss case on the existing tranche is ~$2.9B. We deduct ~$2-2.5B (~$0.5/share).

memo.variant_view: The variant view is modest, and it cuts both ways. Against the options market we are more constructive: its implied 12-month median is ~$364 with P(gain) 54%, while our blended target is $390 with P(gain) 60%, because the agents give credit for ~2x EPS growth at a compressed ~16-17x NTM multiple that the market is not paying for today. Against the sell side we are far more cautious: 38 analysts rate it Strong Buy with a median target of $525.5 (mean $517), which in effect capitalizes management's >$30 FY28 EPS at ~18-20x. We underwrite LSEG's $25.86 and a discount for six-customer concentration, Google's move toward MediaTek and the XPV overhang. So this is not a contrarian call. It is a 'consensus earnings, de-rated multiple' call that is roughly half-way between options pricing and the Street.

valuation.methods: The research target (12m) of $407 is the mean of five independent agents ($391-425), valued as of Sep 2027. Legs: (1) P/E on NTM (mostly FY28) EPS of $24.7-26.5 at 16.5-17x = $420-439 (40-60% weight); (2) FCF yield of 5-5.5% on ~$97-122B NTM/FY28 FCF = $388-441; (3) DCF at 10% WACC, 3% terminal growth = $311-373 (agents 1 and 5); (4) SOTP with AI at 16x after-tax earnings = $333-388 (agents 2 and 3). EV-based legs deduct $35.4B net debt ($59.419B debt less $23.975B cash) and ~$2-2.5B expected XPV loss; all use 4.94B non-GAAP diluted shares. $407 is ~16x NTM EPS of ~$25.5, dividends (~$2.60/yr) excluded. The published $390.49 target is the median of the blended distribution (67% options market, 33% agents after calibration), below the research target (12m) because of the 44-58% volatility and the fat left tail. Expected value is $435; quartiles $291 / $522.

catalysts.event: Micron fiscal Q4 FY26 results (after close)
catalysts.why_it_moves: HBM pricing and supply read-through: memory-heavy XPUs are the main reason Broadcom's gross margin is guided down to ~73%, and HBM/substrate tightness can shift XPU revenue across quarters.
catalysts.watch: HBM4 pricing for 2027, sold-out commentary and capacity adds; higher HBM prices are bullish for AI demand but negative for AVGO gross margin.

catalysts.event: Anthropic public S-1 / institutional roadshow / possible IPO pricing
catalysts.why_it_moves: Anthropic is expected to be Broadcom's largest XPU customer in 2027 and the tenant behind the XPV lease Backstop (max ~$29B) and the $42B convertible-note facility. A funded, well-received IPO de-risks both the 5 GW TPU ramp and the credit overhang; a delay or weak pricing does the opposite. The S-1 will also disclose the size and terms of the compute commitments.
catalysts.watch: Public S-1 filing; disclosed compute commitments to Google/Broadcom and the Fluidstack/XPV leases; pricing versus the $965B Series H mark; any delay announcement.

catalysts.event: Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon Q3 results and first 2027 capex guides
catalysts.why_it_moves: Google TPU and Meta MTIA spending is Broadcom revenue. 2027 capex growth is expected to slow from ~79% to ~35%; a weaker guide would hit the multiple, a stronger one would support the $115B FY27 plan.
catalysts.watch: 2027 capex ranges, Alphabet TPU commentary (Broadcom vs MediaTek), Meta MTIA scale-up, any mention of data-center power/shell delays.

catalysts.event: China SASAC decision on Broadcom switches in state-backed data centres
catalysts.why_it_moves: The survey found Broadcom switches in up to ~90% of state-owned data centres and is also examining bundling. Informal 'domestic chips' guidance would cut China networking sales and add an antitrust-style overhang.
catalysts.watch: Reports of informal procurement guidance favouring Huawei/H3C/Ruijie, any SAMR bundling probe, and management quantifying China switch exposure.

catalysts.event: XPV follow-on debt deal (~$70-80B, reported) for Anthropic/OpenAI compute
catalysts.why_it_moves: Pricing and demand for the next tranche is the market's cleanest read on XPV credit risk; a new tranche also enlarges Broadcom's contingent exposure.
catalysts.watch: Deal size, spread, Broadcom's Backstop terms on the new tranche, rating-agency and credit-strategist commentary.

catalysts.event: Nvidia Q3 FY27 results
catalysts.why_it_moves: Sector sentiment on AI capex; AVGO has traded with the group since the September 'pace the frontier' sell-off.
catalysts.watch: Data-center guide versus the $108B revenue outlook; comments on customer ASIC competition and power constraints.

catalysts.event: Broadcom Q4 FY26 results, FY27 outlook and annual dividend increase (after close; date from aggregators, not yet announced by Broadcom)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The first hard checkpoint on the $115B FY27 AI plan. The Q3 print fell despite a beat because the Q4 guide was light; this print sets the Q1 FY27 guide and the tone for the $230B FY28 target.
catalysts.watch: Q4 AI revenue vs $21.7B guide and total vs $34.8B; Q1 FY27 AI guide (needs a run-rate consistent with ~$29B/quarter average for $115B); explicit reaffirmation of $115B/$230B and >$30 FY28 EPS; gross margin vs ~73%; XPV Backstop balance and any convertible notes issued; Google share comments; dividend raise.

catalysts.event: Hyperscaler Q4 results and finalized 2027 capex budgets
catalysts.why_it_moves: Locks in the capex envelope that funds FY27 XPU and networking shipments.
catalysts.watch: Year-over-year 2027 capex growth versus the ~35% expectation; Google TPU generation vendor split.

catalysts.event: Broadcom Q1 FY27 results
catalysts.why_it_moves: First quarter of the FY27 ramp: shows whether the Anthropic TPU 8i (5 GW) and OpenAI (1.3 GW) deployments start on schedule.
catalysts.watch: AI revenue run-rate versus the $115B path, gross margin trend, 10-Q update on XPV Backstop and note-facility draws.

risks.risk: Frontier-lab deployment or funding slip (Anthropic, OpenAI) pushes FY27 AI revenue well under $115B and turns XPV into a live credit issue.
risks.signpost: Anthropic IPO delayed or priced well below the Series H mark; OpenAI stays private into late 2027; any convertible notes issued under the $42B facility in a 10-Q; management softening '$115B' to timing language on land/power/shell readiness.

risks.risk: Google moves TPU volume to MediaTek faster than Macquarie's 95% -> 80% -> 65% (2026-28) path.
risks.signpost: Alphabet or supply-chain reports of MediaTek winning next-gen TPU volume; Broadcom declining to quantify Google revenue for FY27; further sell-side FY28 EPS cuts.

risks.risk: The multiple compresses further on AI-capex digestion fears (the 12-20x range explains most of the outcome spread).
risks.signpost: 2027 hyperscaler capex growth guided below ~35%; a renewed 'pace the frontier' policy push; the stock closing below the $289.96 52-week low while estimates hold.

risks.risk: Gross-margin dilution and China: memory-heavy XPUs/racks and a SASAC substitution push.
risks.signpost: Gross margin guided below ~73% for Q1 FY27; formal or informal SASAC procurement guidance against Broadcom switches.

what_changes_our_mind: The Q4 FY26 print (~Dec 10) guides Q1 FY27 AI revenue below a run-rate consistent with $115B, or management stops reaffirming the $230B FY28 target.
Anthropic's IPO is pulled or priced sharply below its $965B private mark, or a 10-Q shows convertible notes issued under the $42B facility or a payment under the lease Backstop.
2027 hyperscaler capex guides (late Oct / early Feb) come in flat to down, or Alphabet confirms a majority of next-gen TPU volume moving to MediaTek.

memo.title: BKNG: low-conviction Long sized for portfolio fit. Trough multiple and buybacks against an unresolved AI-agent overhang
memo.call_reason: Low-conviction, portfolio-fit Long. The target ($179.61) is above the $163.31 price, but the supervisor rated sizing conviction low (0.52), below the medium minimum. The owner took it anyway on 2026-10-01 as a deliberate exception, replacing Microchip, because it lifted the book's forward Sharpe the most (0.594 to 0.66) and correlates only about 0.10 with AVGO.
memo.one_liner: Booking trades at about 13.7x NTM consensus, at its 2022 trough, while buybacks shrink the share count 6-8% a year. That supports a $179.61 12-month target and a $194 research target (12m). The stock-specific edge is thin (an idiosyncratic de-rating has beaten SPY only half the time), so this is a capped 6-share position held mainly because it diversifies a book otherwise driven by AI semis and power.

thesis.point: 1. The valuation already prices a lot of damage.
thesis.evidence: At $163.31 BKNG is about 13.7x NTM consensus (FY2027 EPS $12.37, 33 analysts, flat over 90 days). The supervisor rebuilt realized-forward P/E history: the ex-COVID median is about 19x, with troughs of about 15x (2011-12), 16.7x (2018) and 11.3-13.8x (2022). The FCF yield is about 7.8% on LTM FCF of $9.54B. A flat multiple plus EPS growth alone gets to about $180 by Sep 2027.

thesis.point: 2. Buybacks turn mid-single-digit volume growth into mid-teens EPS growth.
thesis.evidence: There were 751.4M shares on Jul 27, 2026. About 22M were retired in Q2, and $14.5B of authorization remains, so the count shrinks 6-8% a year. Q2 FCF was $3.6B (+16% y/y). FY2026 consensus EPS of $10.45 is +14.6% on FY2025's split-adjusted $9.12.

thesis.point: 3. The AI-agent fear is running ahead of the numbers.
thesis.evidence: The CEO says AI-generated traffic is 'significantly below 1%' of room nights. In Q2 room nights grew +5% and marketing was 4.7% of gross bookings, with no sign yet of lost share or rising marketing intensity. Booking is a hotel partner in Google's agentic AI Mode and has an ad deal with OpenAI. The Sep 23 sell-off came from Expedia's Meta Muse deal, which is a headline and not a number in Booking's results.

memo.variant_view: There is no real variant view against the Street, and our target is below it. Our $179.61 target sits under every one of the 35 analyst targets (weighted median $234.34, low $188), because we do not assume the market closes the AI discount within 12 months: the forecast median ($178-180) is below our own $194 research target (12m). Our view differs mainly from the options market. The options-only distribution centres at $165.64 with P(gain) 0.513, against our blended P(gain) of 0.591 and expected value of $190.51. The research adds roughly 8pp of upside probability from the trough multiple and the buyback math. That gap is modest and the supervisor treats it as thin edge, so the case for owning BKNG here rests as much on what it does for the book as on beating consensus.

valuation.methods: Supervisor's reconciled research target (12m) is $194 (agents $187-198, mean $194.4). It blends two methods. P/E (weight 0.6): NTM EPS at Sep 2027 of about $13.3 (FY2027 consensus $12.37 less 2%, FY2028 about +12.5-13%) x 14.5x = $193. FCF yield (weight 0.4): FY2027 FCF of about $10.45B over about 700M average diluted shares = about $14.9 per share at a 7.6% yield = $196. It then deducts about $1-2 for expected legal costs. The 12-month target is $179.61, the median of the blended distribution, which puts 0.67 weight on the options market and 0.33 on research. The expected value is $190.51 and P(gain) is 0.591.

Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. agents.reasoning: Delta refresh of my 2026-10-02 file. I re-checked filings first. EDGAR shows no 8-K, 10-Q or proxy since Aug 10; the only new filing is an Oct 2 Form 4. So I re-opened and confirmed every reported figure that feeds my fair value at source: the Q2 8-K, the 10-Q, the Q2 call transcript, and the June 5 and Aug 10 8-Ks. The only company releases are the Oct 6 Constellation PPA (890 MW of uprates, 20 years; a separate 2,700 MW, 15-year supply deal; first uprate 2028; cost undisclosed) and the Sep 30/Oct 1 Gemini 4 Argon preview (Fairwind-only, no GA date). Neither changes a 12-month number. Neither does the stock's move: +1.2% Oct 2-6, in line with QQQ's +1.3%. What did change is consensus. CY2027 EPS is now $15.10 (S&P Global; 24/7 Wall St shows $14.47 to $15.10 in 90 days), against $14.84 in my last file. MarketScreener carries CY2028 at $17.89. I also built the 10-peer comp set my prior file lacked, on one CY2027 basis. Its median is 19.6x P/E and 11.9x EV/EBITDA; GOOGL is at 23.0x all-in and 22.0x core. I now apply 21x core, down from 21.5x and anchored to that peer set, to CY2028E EPS of $17.0 (consensus less about 5% for 2027-capex D&A, sized from the standing capex view: Big-4 2027 base +47%), up from $16.5. With about $15/share of stakes, the P/E leg is $372. The SOTP is unchanged at $348. The blend is $362, against $361. The ladder uses median ≈ fair value $362 (+4%), a fat-tailed lognormal mixture (27% sigma at 70%, 40% at 30%, about 31% effective vs 32% realised), and P(≥ spot) of 0.55. The scenario mean is $368 (22/53/25 at $245/$368/$475), consistent with right skew. Thesis break stays $255. For one month, the Q3 print is about 97% inside the window, two-sided, centred at about $349. Lane: 9 of the 15 non-comp sources are primary (60%). The 30 data pages behind the comp table (3 per peer, required by the 2026-10-03 peer rule) are not counted. No option data was used.

agents.reasoning: Delta refresh from 2026-10-02. No new filings. The Q3 print is now fixed for Oct 28, inside the 1-month window. The stock rose 1.2%, matching QQQ and the mega-cap peers, so price action since 10-02 carries no GOOGL-specific information. Industry read-through stays constructive for Cloud and TPU: the Constellation 20-year 890 MW uprate PPA plus 2,700 MW supply deal shows Alphabet contracting power years ahead (supplier-side confirmation of a long build-out, and a Gemini Enterprise customer win); Marvell's investor day lifted ASIC peers on the custom-silicon share thesis; Wells Fargo now sees $9.2B and $11.5B of external TPU sales in Q3/Q4. Gemini 4 Argon tops the Arena leaderboard and Polymarket moved Google to 42.5% for best model at end-2026. The ad side is unchanged: the last tracker (Tinuiti Q2) shows click-led Search growth with CPC +1%, and Meta and Amazon ads outgrew Search. Valuation: consensus FY27 rose to $14.95 and FY28 is verified at $17.89. I take $17.5 after a D&A adjustment for the standing capex view (Alphabet 2027 capex ~10% above consensus). The new 11-peer set gives a 21.8x median next-FY P/E; GOOGL's ~22.1x core multiple is already at the median and its FY28 growth matches the mega-cap median, so I apply 21.8x with no premium: P/E leg $399. I corrected my SOTP to deduct unallocated costs and moved it to the 2028 horizon: $326. Blend 60/40 = $370 (+6.4%). Distribution: two-piece lognormal, median ~$366, sigma ~0.30 up / 0.34 down (realised vol 32%), with fatter tails for regulatory and capex outcomes. The scenario mean ($375) is close to the ladder mean (~$379). Thesis break $245 (~15x core FY27, Baidu-to-Netflix territory). Research limits: Alpha Vantage was rate-limited, Twelve Data estimates are paywalled, DCD and Benzinga returned 403, and the Tinuiti Q3 report is not yet out. I did not use Anthropic stake-size claims (not disclosed in Alphabet filings) in any number.

agents.reasoning: Skeptic lane. Starting facts (filings): Q2-26 revenue $119.8B (+24%), operating income $40.8B, Cloud $24.8B (+82%) with $8.8B OI, Cloud backlog $513.9B [1][2]. What the consensus may be underweighting: (1) Earnings quality. H1-26 pretax income $216.2B includes $135.9B of equity-security gains (SpaceX IPO and other marks; $94.1B of SpaceX stock, mostly locked up [2][42]) [9][1], so trailing P/E of ~17x is misleading. On ex-gains consensus the stock is 23.2x CY27 [14]. (2) Cash. Q2 FCF -$5.9B, TTM $53.3B [1]. Consensus FCF is $8.4B in 2026 and -$36.7B in 2027 on capex of $201.7B and $301.0B [15], consistent with the standing AI-capex view (Alphabet 2027 consensus $285-357B) [40]. Purchase commitments jumped to $707B [3]. (3) Funding mix. Buybacks went from $13.2B in Q2-25 to zero [1]. Alphabet sold 58M Class A/C shares (net $20.5B) plus $10B to Berkshire, $19B of 6.25% mandatory convertibles, and set up a $40B ATM [4][5][6], plus $45B of bonds in Feb/Aug [7][8][39]. (4) Credit is pricing more risk. On like-for-like tenors, new-issue spreads widened from Feb to Aug: 10y T+63 -> T+85, 40y T+95 -> T+130, despite unchanged AA+/Aa2 ratings [7][8]. The Feb sterling deal included a 2126 century bond at gilts +120bp [41]. That is a mild, not alarming, signal. (5) Concentration and circularity. Anthropic reportedly accounts for over 40% of the backlog [31], and Google backstops financing of Anthropic's TPU purchases [32]. These are press reports (The Information, via Silicon UK), used here only to size bear-case probability, not as valuation inputs. (6) Sentiment is crowded: 0 sells and 4 holds out of 55 analysts; insiders sold ~$8.7M and bought $0 over 3 months [37]. Visible Form 4s are routine 10b5-1 or vesting [11][12][13], so this is not a red flag. Alt-data and markets: StatCounter puts Google at 89.94% of worldwide search in Sep-26 [35]. On Kalshi (via Octagon, Oct 2, week of Oct 5), 'Above 20.5%' Google share of OpenRouter text-model requests traded ~75% and 'Above 19.9%' 97%, with 30,430 contracts on the latter [36]. That reads as a solid but not dominant AI-model position. Privacy litigation remains a recurring cost (shareholder proponents cite a $425.7M privacy jury verdict [38]; PriceRunner $2.1B damages and the $5.2B EU Android payment in Q2-Q3 [3]). What weakens the bear case: the ad tech remedy decision rejected the AdX divestiture and imposed a 6-year behavioral decree [27][28][29][30], removing the largest structural legal tail. The balance sheet remains AA+. Operating momentum is real. Valuation: P/E (21.8x, between the all-peer median 19.8x and the US median 23.5x) on haircut NTM EPS gives $360. EV/EBITDA at the peer median (10.5x) gives $320. Blended fair value is $346, about 0.5% below spot. Scenarios: 257/348/440 at 25/50/25 (mean ~$348). The ladder is a lognormal mixture around those (sigma 0.22/0.17/0.17), giving a log-sd of ~0.27 and median ~$348. memo.title: GOOGL: Long, small. 25% core EPS growth at 22x with the Anthropic/SpaceX stakes as a free option; target $371.53 (+8.4%)
memo.call_reason: The published target ($371.53) is above the $342.75 close, P(gain) is 0.59 and sizing conviction is medium, so this is a small, staged long. It is not a special situation.
memo.one_liner: Alphabet trades at about 21x forward core EPS while FY2027 consensus EPS grows about 25% with revisions running 8 up to 1 down, Cloud grows 82% on a $514B backlog, and roughly $13-15/sh of SpaceX/Anthropic stakes carry a November IPO option. The edge is modest (+8% to target against 36% implied vol), so we buy 2 shares in two tranches around the Q3 print and keep the stop at $256.52.

thesis.point: Earnings compound at a multiple that already prices in the capex debate.
thesis.evidence: FY2027 consensus core EPS is about $14.92 (+25%), with 8 upward and 1 downward revision in 30 days. NTM core EPS of about $16.2-16.9 at the horizon, at about 22x, gives $356-372 before stakes. The ~$257B 2027 capex consensus is already in that multiple.

thesis.point: Cloud is now a second profit engine, not an option.
thesis.evidence: Q2 2026 Cloud revenue grew about 82% with a $514B backlog, and TPU system sales to third parties begin in 2027. Backlog conversion is what supports FY2027 numbers while Search decelerates.

thesis.point: The equity stakes and base rates add a right tail at little cost.
thesis.evidence: SpaceX is about $82B (551M shares at $148.68, $14.1B locked until Q3 2027) and Anthropic is carried at $124.3B on a $47.6B cost. A reported November IPO at about $2T would add roughly $5-11/sh after tax. Separately, 9 of 10 prior 15% drawdowns were higher a year later; the one exception required EPS to fall 19%.

memo.variant_view: There is no strong variant view; this is a modest long. We sit between two consensuses. Our $371.53 target is well below the sell side (49 analysts, mean $425.45, median $425, range $310-515, Strong Buy), because we apply about 22x NTM core EPS and haircut for 2027 capex, negative FCF and the $84.75B equity program, which the Street's ~$425 largely looks through. We are slightly above the options market: its distribution centers on $358.96 with P(gain) 0.554 and a 15th percentile of $247.69, against our $371.53, P(gain) 0.593 and $256.52. Our small premium to the options market comes from the fact-checked EPS revision trend and the stake/IPO optionality. The difference is about 3.5% of price, which is not enough to call it a mispricing.

valuation.methods: Supervisor-reconciled research target (12m) of $367 (range across five agents $360-375). The main method is NTM core P/E: about 22x on NTM core EPS of about $16.2-16.9 at the Sept 2027 horizon gives $356-372. Added to that are about $13-15/sh of after-tax stake value (SpaceX corrected to about $82B; Anthropic at its $124.3B carrying value) plus about $4-5/sh of probability-weighted Anthropic IPO uplift. A rolled-forward SOTP (about $370) is the cross-check. DCF cross-checks at $313-340 reflect the ~$257B 2027 capex consensus and are weighted about 20%. The published target of $371.53 is the median of the blended options/forecaster distribution, weighted 67% market and 33% forecasters; the expected value is $391.56 (+14.2%).
