agents.reasoning: Round 2 revision after supervisor fact-check. Fundamentals: Jun-26 quarter sales $1.485B (+38% y/y), Sep-26 guide $1.603B mid (+40% y/y), EPS $0.91-0.95, GM 66-67%; strongest bookings in ~4 years continued through July-August across all units (Citi TMT, 2026-09-09). Supervisor corrections I accept: (1) my 'ordering inside lead time' late-cycle signal was overstated - CFO sees no double ordering, distributor inventory is lean at 25 days (decade range 17-43), internal lead times steady, lead-time stretch is at outsourced AI-constrained capacity; GM guided flat 66-67% through FY27. I therefore cut bear weight from 25% to 20% and raised bear price to $52. I keep a meaningful bear weight because my horizon ends Sep-2027, when the upcycle will be mature and the stock will trade on FY29 - the risk moves later rather than disappearing. (2) Net-debt paydown is ~$250-300M/qtr (June qtr ~$170M), so Sep-2027 net debt ~$3.8B not $3.6B, trimming EV/EBITDA by ~$0.5/sh. (4) Required FCF yield lowered to 5.2% vs peers ON 4.9%/NXPI 4.7%. Share count 574-575M confirmed. Net: fair value $84 -> $85, ~8% above spot $78.69 (analyst mean target ~$100-108 treated as optimistic evidence). Distribution: mixture of a main lognormal (median ~$89, sigma 0.39, weight 85%) and a cycle-turn component (median ~$60, sigma 0.38, weight 15%), giving a median ~$84.5 and P(>=79) 0.56; sigma below 50% realized vol (inflated by the 2025-26 rebound) but above a typical large-cap given beta ~1.7. Scenario mix 20/55/25 at $52/$86/$122 gives mean ~$88, consistent with a right-skewed lognormal around the $84-85 median. No option data used; research limited to 2 extra queries this round.

memo.variant_view: There is no real variant view versus the Street on direction; our view differs on the multiple, and the Street is well above us. Our weighted set of 22 analyst targets (as of 2026-10-13, from MarketBeat; consensus rating Buy) has a weighted median of $95, a weighted mean of $102.04 and a range of $69-125. That implies 20.7x and 22.3x FY28 consensus (95 / 4.58; 102.04 / 4.58). The S&P Global consensus on StockAnalysis is higher still: 26 analysts, average $107.84, median $108, range $80-135 (2026-10-14). Our forecasters use 18.5-19x NTM, because at the Oct-2027 horizon the market will be pricing FY29 on a mature upcycle, with the 10-yr Treasury at 5.21% (2026-10-13). The options market on its own is less constructive than we are: median $71.93, P(gain) 0.48, 15th percentile $42.98. Our forecasters on their own are more constructive: median $92.56, P(gain) 0.70. The published blend (0.67 market, 0.33 forecasters) gives a $78.92 median and P(gain) 0.55. Our edge over the options market is about 7 points of P(gain) (0.55 vs 0.48) and rests on the lean channel and the flat-GM guide, which is too little to override the book's exclusion.

valuation.methods: The research target (12m) of $85 (supervisor; agents $83-86, mean $84.3) blends three methods. (1) P/E, weight 0.5: 18.75x x ~$4.60 NTM EPS at Sep-2027 = $86.25 (estimate; consensus FY28 $4.58 rolled forward, less a light cycle haircut; 575M non-GAAP diluted shares). (2) FCF yield, weight 0.3, equity basis: ~$2.45-2.6B FY28 FCF at a 5.0-5.2% required yield = $85.2-87.0 (2.45 / 0.05 / 0.575; 2.6 / 0.052 / 0.575; FCF ~33% of ~$7.4B sales, Q1 FY27 FCF margin 33.5%). (3) EV/EBITDA, weight 0.2: (16 x ~$3.2B - ~$3.8B Sep-2027 net debt) / 0.575 = $82.4. The supervisor harmonized this leg to 16x from agents 1-4's 14-15.5x (agent 5 already used 16x), which double-counted the derating. Blend: 0.5 x 86.25 + 0.3 x 86 + 0.2 x 82.4 = $85.4, rounded to $85. Scenarios: bear $52 (20-22%), base $86-88 (53-55%), bull $118-125 (25%). Published 12-month distribution (2026-10-13): median (target) $78.92, mean $87.87 (+18.5%), 25th/75th percentile $56.46/$108.81. The ~2.45% dividend is on top. The research passed the citation gate on 2026-10-14 (clean: 78 checked, 11 fixed); no fix changed a number. TRIAL STANDARD MODEL, shown beside the published target and not the target: a standard model built on 2026-10-14 from the same research gives a model target of $85.40 at the research date's $78.69 spot (+8.5%; +15.2% against today's $74.16, derived 85.40 / 74.16), and research target (12m) $85.32 = 0.5 x $86.25 (P/E 18.75x on $4.60 NTM EPS) + 0.3 x $85.20 (5.0% FCF yield on $4.26/share) + 0.2 x $83.19 (16x EV/EBITDA). Bear/base/bull are $51.71/$85.32/$119.43 at 20/55/25%. Caveat: the 18.75x P/E sits at the top of, slightly above, the ~13.7-18.5x NTM P/E range of NXPI and ON (rebuilt by the citation gate from 2026-09-25 closes and StockAnalysis consensus EPS, time-weighted NTM), so the model leans on the high end of peer multiples. trade.entry: No entry. For reference only, if the exclusion were lifted: the supervisor's plan was medium conviction, max 5% of the book, in two tranches (half at once, half after the Q2 FY27 print, ~2026-11-05, estimated).
trade.exit_or_add: There is nothing to exit. A buy would need two things. First, the exclusion lifted: it is a book-construction decision from 2026-10-01 (MCHP moves too much with AVGO; model correlation 0.38 to AVGO and 0.39 to NVDA, both holdings; BKNG took the slot). Second, a gate-clean re-run after the Q2 FY27 print that keeps the target clearly above spot. The published thesis-break stop is $55 (~12x FY28 consensus: 55 / 4.58 = 12.0) and the take-profit is $108.81 (the 75th percentile).

what_changes_our_mind: Q2 FY27 (~2026-11-05, estimated): GM at 66-67% with a December guide at or above seasonal and distributor inventory near 25 days would strengthen the research case. GM below 66% or a guide implying a sequential decline would mean the cycle is rolling before mid-2027.

A December or January pre-announcement above guidance, as on 2025-12-02 and 2026-01-05, plus a buyback-restart signal would move us toward the $95 weighted analyst median. Distributor inventory rising materially from 25 days, or management citing destocking, would move us toward the $52 bear case.

For the book, the exclusion is the binding constraint. If MCHP's correlation to AVGO/NVDA falls, or AVGO leaves the book, a re-run with the target still above spot would make it buyable. A close below $55 ends the thesis.

agents.reasoning: Per-share figures are per CURRENT pre-split share (today's Class A share plus the Class C share it gets in the Jan-2027 dividend; 8-K 2026-10-21); EV is unchanged by the dividend. Evidence, mostly primary: Q3-26 release, 10-Q and call; Q2-26 call; nine prior releases for the guidance record. The core is strong: revenue +26% (impressions +10%, price +14%), Q4 guide $73-76B (+22-27%), and Meta beat the top of its range in 6 of 8 quarters. The debate is cost: FY26 expenses $175-179B (incl. $12.3B legal), capex $135-145B, $454.5B of non-cancelable commitments ($121.4B due 2027), management 'investing aggressively' in 2027, and RL loss ~$15B. Driver build: FY27 revenue $312B (at consensus) from impressions +9% and price +10% plus new AI revenue; FoA margin 51.6% FY25 -> 37.8% FY27 -> 34.5% FY28 as D&A rises with capex that follows the AI capex file ($192B, $236B; above street). FY27 EPS ~$32 (~5% below consensus $33.9). Valuation: SOTP $750 (FoA 16.5x NTM EBIT, RL -$25B), P/E 20x $691, EV/EBITDA 10x $681 -> research target (12m) $715.83, +11% vs $642.62. Scenarios: bear $409 (25%), base $716 (50%), bull $1,019 (25%). Ladder: 75% this scenario mix (within-scenario vol 17-18%) plus 25% a market-anchored lognormal (median $650, sigma 33%, about the stock's 43% realized vol trimmed for non-earnings periods), since price is the best single forecast. That gives a median of ~$697 and P(>= $643) = 0.59. Not driver-linked: the RL venture value (-$25B), the litigation and investment adjustments, and RL revenue. Research limits: the Q3 call transcript was reached at a content_files URL; no option data was used.

tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. thesis.evidence: 53,196,918 shares x $135.17 + $265.3M pro forma net debt at June 30 (8-K/A Ex.99.1 of Oct 7: $43.4M current + $276.0M long-term debt - $54.1M cash; derived) = ~$7.46B EV over ~$535-555M NTM EBITDA (supervisor estimate). memo.variant_view: We sit between the Street and the options market. Analysts (9, Strong Buy) have a median target of $301 (low $260) on StockAnalysis, and our recency-weighted median of the individual targets is $293.67 (as of Oct 20); several were set before the Oct 1 spin and on premium multiples; our research target (12m) of $200 uses 17x EBITDA, a ~16% discount to peers justified by ~11% single-customer concentration and below-peer DC margins [1][3][18][22]. The options market's own 12-month median is $134.66, roughly today's price (it gives a 44% chance of closing above the Oct 21 mark of $149.78 and ~50% above today's $135.17); our research is more constructive because DC growth is guided and contracted [1][17][19]. The published target $161.51 weights the options market 67% and research 33% [1]. The variant is modest: we are not calling the Street's $290s, only that the stock is pricing an AI-capex down-cycle that the latest hyperscaler data (Meta raising the low end of 2026 capex) does not show [1][11].

valuation.methods: Research target (12m) $200 (supervisor, after the Oct 6 citation audit): Oct-2027 NTM RemainCo EBITDA ~$665M (median of five agent builds, corporate -$80M) x 17x = EV $11.3B, less ~$280M at-close net debt, over 54.0M diluted shares = ~$204; P/E ($665M - $85M D&A - $15M interest) x 0.76 / 54.0M = ~$7.95 x 24.5x = ~$195; blended 60/40 = ~$200. Agent research targets (12m) $175-212 (four of five at $198-212); probability-weighted scenarios bear $105-125 / base $180-212 / bull $280-315 at 25/50/25. The published 12-month target $161.51 blends the options-implied distribution (67%, median $134.66) with the research distribution (33%, median $201.33); expected value $194.93 [1][3][4][5][6][7][8].

tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.

Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.

tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM GAAP EPS at horizon ~$4.19 (model; consensus FY27 $3.80 / FY28 $4.52) x 18x (single-basis peer median 20.4x, gate-corrected from a mixed-basis 22.4x; NFLX today 18.2x NTM)

inputs_detail.derivation: 8-peer median NTM P/E 22.4x: peers.md DIS 15.2, FOXA 11.1, WMG 18.5, META 22.2, AMZN 28.2, TKO 35.4, plus GOOGL 340.27/14.97 = 22.7x on FY2027 (its FY2026 EPS carries stake gains, peers.md note) and SPOT 526.12/17.28 = 30.4x (Nasdaq consensus, my arithmetic). NFLX's own post-print NTM multiple: 64.85 / (Q4'26 guide $0.67 + Q1-Q3'27 consensus 0.93+0.98+0.98 = $3.56) = 18.2x. 18x holds today's discount (~20%) to the median: NFLX's FY28/FY27 consensus EPS growth (+19%, 4.52/3.80) is below the next-year growth of META (+23.5%), AMZN (+32.7%) (peers.md) and SPOT (+26.0%, 17.28/13.71), and US TV-time share is slipping to YouTube (Nielsen via AdWave); I have no evidenced catalyst for a re-rating within 12 months, so round 1's 19x is cut to 18x. Gate correction (2026-10-21, mixed basis): the 8-peer median mixed the run table's NTM fiscal-year blends with GOOGL and SPOT on calendar FY2027 alone. On one basis (peers.md NTM fiscal-year blend of Nasdaq.com/Zacks consensus EPS, Zacks basis for every name) the median is 20.4x: FOXA 11.1, DIS 15.2, WMG 18.5, META 22.2, AMZN 28.2, TKO 35.4 -> (18.5 + 22.2) / 2 = 20.35. GOOGL is dropped (its Zacks FY2026 EPS 20.55 includes non-operating stake gains); SPOT is out of the run table (EUR reporter) and on the same blend is 526.08 / (0.504 x 13.71 + 0.496 x 17.28 = 15.48) = 34.0x, which would make a 7-name median of 22.2x. The 18x multiple itself is unchanged (judgment).

memo.title: NFLX: small two-step long in a de-rated cash compounder at ~18x 2027 EPS; the Oct 20 print and the January 2027 guide settle the engagement debate
memo.call_reason: The published 12-month target of $75.49 is 8.5% above the $69.58 close and the research target (12m) of $80.00 is 15.0% above it, at medium conviction; size is capped by the supervisor at ~8% because the engagement debate is unresolved and earnings are three weeks out.
memo.one_liner: Netflix has de-rated to ~18x 2027 consensus EPS on an engagement scare that has not yet reached churn (2% vs a 4% industry average) or pricing, while recurring FCF of ~$11.3-11.7B and a ~3-4% annual share shrink keep compounding per-share value. We buy 11 shares in two tranches around the Oct 20 print, target $75.49 / research target (12m) $80, take profit $97.77, stop at the $51 thesis break.

thesis.point: 1. Per-share cash compounding is intact and is being bought back cheaply.
thesis.evidence: Recurring 2026 FCF is ~$11.3-11.7B (the $11B pre-fee guide incl. the ~$700M Brazil deposit, vs $12.5B including the after-tax WBD fee), implying ~$13.0-13.5B in 2027. Net debt is only $5.24B (A2/A), and Q2 buybacks retired 52.9M shares, shrinking the 4.164B count ~3-4% a year.

thesis.point: 2. Monetisation shows no damage from the engagement debate yet.
thesis.evidence: Antenna July churn is 2% vs a 4% average for major services; the 2026 upfront nearly doubled ad commitments and the ad tier passed 250M monthly active viewers, with ads ~$3B in 2026. The fall season (~40% of annual gross adds) is the next test.

thesis.point: 3. The multiple already discounts a lot; the bar for the print is low.
thesis.evidence: At $69.58 the stock trades ~18x 2027 consensus EPS of $3.82 with 2028 at $4.56, near Wells Fargo's 15x bear multiple ($57 PT) after Wells Fargo and HSBC downgrades in September. Our research target (12m) of $80 needs only ~19x NTM EPS of ~$4.25 and a 4.5% FCF yield, not a return to the old 30x+.

memo.variant_view: We sit between the two consensus views. The options market's distribution (result.json market_only) is centred at $70.19 with P(gain) 0.51, i.e. it prices no edge; we have $75.49 and P(gain) 0.58 because the forecasters see churn, ad growth and buybacks absorbing the engagement drag. The sell-side is far more bullish (weighted median PT $95, Deutsche Bank upgrade to Buy at $95 on 9/29, Wells Fargo $57 underweight); we stay well below it because peer de-ratings of quality large caps (DIS, PYPL, NKE, ADBE) have a median ~-6% follow-through over the next 12 months, so we do not underwrite a re-rating before the January 2027 guide. The real variant view is modest: the market is treating an engagement metric (Nielsen 7.8% share vs YouTube 14.2%; Wells Fargo ~-4% y/y hours per member in H2'26) as if it were already a revenue problem.

valuation.methods: Supervisor research target (12m) $80 (five forecasters $77-83, mean $80.3) = 60/40 blend of (a) P/E: NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of 0.25x$3.82 + 0.75x$4.56 = $4.38, less ~3% engagement haircut = $4.25, at 19x = ~$81; and (b) FCF: NTM FCF ~$14.5B at a 4.5% yield, less $5.24B net debt, over ~4.08B diluted shares = ~$77.7. The published 12-month target ($75.49, the median of the blended market/forecaster distribution) sits below the research target (12m) because the options market centres near spot; take profit $97.77 is the 75th percentile, stop $51 is the thesis break (~13.4x 2027 EPS, ~6.6% FCF yield).

catalysts.event: Paramount Skydance closes its WBD acquisition (all regulatory conditions met in Aug; 12-state AG settlement Sep 21)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Creates a combined HBO Max/Paramount+ rival with ~$80B of debt; integration plans and bundling/pricing signal how hard it will compete for subscribers and content.
catalysts.watch: Streaming bundle/pricing announcements, content-spend guidance and leverage of the combined company.

catalysts.event: First Nielsen Gauge on the recalibrated methodology (ARF DASH universe), covering the start of the fall TV season
catalysts.why_it_moves: Nielsen share (7.8% vs YouTube 14.2% in July) is the core of the bear case; a further drop under the new method would be read as confirmation even though it is a methodology break.
catalysts.watch: Netflix share of TV time vs the July 7.8% and YouTube's lead; any restatement of history under the new method.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results and Q4 guide (letter 1:01pm PT, video interview 1:45pm PT)
catalysts.why_it_moves: First print since the September downgrades; the Q4 guide and any 2027 framing set the growth path the multiple hangs on. Q2's slight beat with a lower outlook sent the stock down after hours.
catalysts.watch: Revenue vs $12.86B guide, 33.2% operating margin, EPS $0.82; Q4 guide vs the $51.2B / 31.5% FY26 plan; engagement and ad-revenue commentary; Q3 buyback pace and FCF vs the ~$12.5B FY guide; early 2027 growth/margin framing (~10% growth, 33-34% margin needed).

catalysts.event: Antenna churn and sign-up reads through the fall acquisition season
catalysts.why_it_moves: Churn at 2% is the evidence that engagement loss has not reached monetisation; Sep-Dec is ~40% of annual gross adds, so a rise here would validate the bear case.
catalysts.watch: Netflix monthly churn above ~2.5%; gross adds vs prior years; ad-tier mix.

catalysts.event: NFL Thanksgiving Eve game on Netflix (Packers at Rams), first of its kind
catalysts.why_it_moves: Live-sports tentpoles drive sign-ups and ad inventory and counter the engagement narrative; a streaming failure would hurt.
catalysts.watch: Reported viewership, stream stability, ad sell-out.

catalysts.event: Fury vs. Joshua heavyweight fight streamed live on Netflix (reported by trade/fan press, not yet verified in a company release)
catalysts.why_it_moves: A global live event at no extra cost; another engagement and sign-up spike for Q4.
catalysts.watch: Concurrent viewers; Q4 net-add commentary in January.

catalysts.event: NFL Christmas Day doubleheader exclusively on Netflix
catalysts.why_it_moves: Highest-profile ad inventory of the year; supports the ad-scaling leg of the thesis.
catalysts.watch: Viewership vs 2025 Christmas games; advertiser demand.

catalysts.event: Q4 2026 results and first full-year 2027 revenue, margin and FCF guidance
catalysts.why_it_moves: The main re-rating or de-rating event: ~10% 2027 growth with 33-34% margin supports the $80 research target (12m); high-single-digit growth or a flat margin is the bear path toward the $51 thesis break.
catalysts.watch: 2027 revenue growth vs ~10%, operating margin vs 33-34%, 2027 FCF vs ~$13.0-13.5B, buyback size, ad-revenue target.

catalysts.event: H2 2026 'What We Watched' engagement report
catalysts.why_it_moves: Direct test of Wells Fargo's ~-4% y/y hours-per-member call for H2'26.
catalysts.watch: Total hours and hours per member y/y; share of views from top titles.

risks.risk: Engagement erosion reaches churn and pricing power (YouTube and creators taking TV time).
risks.signpost: Antenna churn above ~2.5% for two consecutive months, Netflix share falling further on the recalibrated Gauge, or a weaker take-rate on the next price increase.

risks.risk: The January 2027 guide shows high-single-digit growth and a stalled margin, cutting 2027/28 EPS.
risks.signpost: A Q4 guide on Oct 20 below the implied $51.2B FY26 plan, or 2027 framing under ~10% growth / ~33% margin.

risks.risk: The de-rating persists even if fundamentals hold (peer base rate: median ~-6% follow-through in 12 months).
risks.signpost: Stock fails to rally on a clean Oct 20 print and stays below ~$63 into January.

agents.reasoning: Round 2. Primary documents show an extraordinary ramp: Q2 FY27 revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y), non-GAAP EPS $2.22, Q3 guide $108B, and a call guide of ~70% FY28 revenue growth, supply-constrained, with GM settling at 72-73% (verified verbatim by the supervisor). Today's 19.3x is on $12.00-12.25; the 17x and 14.8x quotes are later windows, so I compress from 19.3x not 17x. I keep 16x (not the supervisor's 16.5x) because by the horizon estimate growth itself decelerates; break-even is 13.5x, so 16x embeds ~2.5 turns of compression. Fair value $270 (+14%), up from $267: the EPS-window fix (+$3 on P/E leg) outweighs the net-cash cut (-$1.8/share before adding back haircut stakes). Scenarios 145/268/370 at 25/50/25 (mean ~$263). Ladder is a 50/50 blend of a lognormal (median $253, sigma 0.42, above 38% realized vol for cycle/event risk) and a scenario mixture, with fat left tail kept: P(>= spot) 59.4%. No option data used; priors not opened.

memo.one_liner: NVDA trades at ~19.5x NTM EPS, a decade low and below AVGO/TSM, with FY28 guided to ~+70% revenue; even after assuming the multiple compresses to 16x we get a $263 research target (12m) and a $268.93 target. The risk is a 2027-28 hyperscaler capex digestion, so we hold 1 share and add only if the Oct 27-30 capex guides and the ~Nov 17-18 Q3 FY27 print confirm demand.

thesis.point: The valuation already prices heavy de-rating: the stock is flat in a year only at ~13.9x Oct-2027 NTM EPS.
thesis.evidence: $238.90 is ~19.5x NTM consensus EPS of $12.00-12.25 (Q3 FY27-Q2 FY28; stockanalysis fwd P/E 19.34x), vs AVGO 20.49x and TSM 20.65x. Consistent Oct-2027 NTM EPS of $17.1 means a flat year needs ~13.9x, a further ~29% de-rating. All five agents assume compression to 16-17x and still reach research targets (12m) of $250-296.

thesis.point: Earnings visibility through FY28 is unusually high and supply-constrained.
thesis.evidence: Q2 FY27 revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y), Data Center $89.0B (+117%), non-GAAP GM 75.0%. The Q3 guide is $108.0B ±2% at 74.0% GM. Management's preliminary FY28 view is ~+70% revenue at 72-73% GM after a 71-72% Q4 trough. $279B of supply and capacity commitments back the ramp.

thesis.point: Customer capex keeps being revised up, and backlogs fund the 2027 ramp.
thesis.evidence: Big-4 2026 capex guides rose from ~$655B to $732.5B during the year, and none was cut. 2027 Big-4 consensus is $934.5B (IO Fund) to $1,029B (S&P), against our base case of $1,080B. Backlogs: MSFT commercial RPO $678B, Google Cloud $513.9B, AWS $496B. Year-ahead consensus drift was +25% to +62% in each of 2024-26.

memo.variant_view: There is no strong variant view against the options market. Our $268.93 target and 0.63 P(gain) sit close to the options-only distribution (target $263.75, P(gain) 0.61, 15th percentile $173.36). Against the sell side we are more cautious: the 50-analyst median target is $315 (range $210-515, Strong Buy), ~17% above ours. The gap is the multiple, not EPS: we assume 16x on Oct-2027 NTM EPS because FY29 growth should slow to low-to-mid teens. Our customer-capex work adds a second gap. At base capture, base-case 2027 capex implies FY28 revenue of ~$647B, 6% below the $687B consensus, and NVIDIA's supply cap (~$700-750B) limits FY28 upside. So we are below the Street on both multiple and FY28 revenue, and in line with options. [sources 9, 11, 12]

valuation.methods: Supervisor research target (12m) $263 is a blend of two legs. P/E (60%): consistent Oct-2027 NTM EPS (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29) of $17.1 = H2 FY28 consensus $8.90 + H1 FY29 ~$8.5 (FY29 +13-15%, ~2% memory-cost haircut), x 16x = $274. FCF yield (40%): $17.1 x 23.9B shares x 72% conversion = $12.3/share at a 5.0% yield = $246, + ~$1 net cash = $247. Agent research targets (12m) $250/$255/$260/$270/$296 (median $260). agent_4 is high on 17x and a 4.5% yield. 16x is ~22% below the AVGO/TSM 20.57x anchor. The published target $268.93 is the median of the blended options-plus-agents distribution. Thesis break $160.

trade.entry: Staged in two tranches. Tranche 1 (1 sh) is done. Tranche 2 (+1 sh, to 2 sh total, ~4.8% of the book, under the supervisor's 5% cap) comes after the ~Nov 17-18 Q3 FY27 results, and only if (a) the Oct 27-30 hyperscaler 2027 capex guides come in at or above the base case in adhoc/nvda_customer_capex.md (Big-4 2027 ~$1,080B), (b) the Q3 print keeps the Q4 guide and the FY28 ~+70% framework intact, and (c) price stays above the $174.61 stop.
trade.exit_or_add: Exit on a close below the stop. The stop is $174.61 (15th percentile). Also exit, whatever the price, if Big-4 2027 guides come in below the ~$935B consensus or the Q4 guide breaks the FY28 ~+70% / 71-72% GM framework. Thesis break is $160. Take profit at $337.15. Trim above ~$303 per the decider ladder. Add to 2 sh only on the conditions above. Without a fresh catalyst the decider's add levels are ~$215 (+1 sh) and ~$205 (to 2 sh above base), each after a news check. [Updated 2026-10-30: the one upside exit is now $241.10, where the 12-month expected value no longer beats the 4% cash sleeve and the model sells every share; any other take-profit figure in this memo is superseded.]

what_changes_our_mind: Big-4 2027 capex guides on Oct 27-30 sum below the ~$935B consensus, or any of the four guides 2027 flat. That breaks the base case and moves us toward exiting rather than adding.
Q3 FY27 (~Nov 17-18): a Q4 guide or commentary implying FY28 growth well below ~+70%, a GM trough below 71%, or DSO above 60 days with FCF conversion still under ~50%.

Upside case: 2027 guides at or above our $1,360B high case together with a FY28 outlook of at least +75%. That would justify the full 3 sh and moving the target toward agent_4's $296 research target (12m).

results.supervisor_summary: AT&T's research target (12m) is $23.16 (+11% from $20.93, plus a 5.3% dividend), the engine value of a driver-led set that the five revised forecasts now bracket ($22.24-24.39 after the gate arithmetic fixes, mean $23.08). The horizon EV/EBITDA stays at the post-SpaceX 6.1x, as Kilian decided; the build sits below management on 2028 (EBITDA +3.4% vs 5%+, FCF $18.5B/$20.0B vs the $19B+/$21B+ floors) because Legacy EBITDA turns negative and ARPU growth fades, while lower D&A and ~5% a year of buybacks keep 2028 EPS at $2.91, above the $2.82 floor. Our checks narrowed small gaps rather than settling a large one, so the ladder stays at the forecasters' mean; the thesis break is $16.5 (cable-like ~5.2x EBITDA). SpaceX headlines (FCC space-coverage vote Oct-29, any site deal) are the near-term risk; a 4-6% position in two tranches fits a book with no telecom exposure.

tax_assumptions._ignore_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: ignore taxes for now (he has money set aside for the liability). Set false to use the tax facts below.
tax_assumptions._future_note: Combined rate you'd expect on today's embedded gains when you'd otherwise sell (15% federal + ~6% state once working). Drives the sell cost and the gain-harvest suggestion.
tax_assumptions._tax_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: taxable account; ~$20,000 internship wages in 2026 plus realized gains; claimed as a dependent by a parent living in CA; full-time student under 24 living in CT. Assumed (not confirmed): domicile stays CA (a student living away at school keeps the parents' domicile, FTB Pub 1031), CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode so CT does not tax investment income; kiddie tax applies (earned income not more than half of his support). Federal 2026 figures from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32; CA brackets are 2025 (FTB Tax News Oct 2025), 2026's not published yet.
tax_assumptions._other_unearned_note: Dividends etc. this year (rough: GOOGL + META dividends). Counts toward the kiddie-tax threshold.
tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.
tax_assumptions._parent_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: parent in NYC, 37% federal bracket. Parent's NY/NYC rates do not apply to Kilian's gains (no NY kiddie tax under Form 8615).
tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

agents.method_text: Driver-led 3-year build (subs x ARPU for wireless and broadband, AC cost and capex drivers; EPS, FCF/share and horizon net debt linked to the drivers) valued at the horizon on NTM figures: 6.2x EV/EBITDA ($23.43, weight 0.5), 8.1x P/E on EPS $2.92 ($24.37, 0.3) and a 12.3% FCF yield on $2.89/share ($24.26, 0.2) = research target (12m) $23.88.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 6.2x NTM EBITDA at the horizon (~$50.6B = 0.19 x FY2027 $48.9B + 0.81 x FY2028 $51.0B from the driver build) less net debt $147.9B, NCI $18.0B, preferred $2.95B, plus Mexico (0.9 x $3.2B), the Forged Fiber stake $3.65B and upper C-band (-$5B x 0.35), over 6,385M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Base: average of year-end 2024 (72,749k) and 2025 (74,214k) postpaid phone subscribers, Q4 2025 Ex.99.2; Sep-30-2026 75,283k and 9M net adds 1,105k, Q3 2026 Ex.99.2 | 2026: average of Dec-2025 74.21M and est. Dec-2026 75.68M (Sep-26 75.28M + Q4 net adds ~0.40M vs 0.42M in Q4 2025) = 74.95M. 2027: net adds 1.2M (vs 1.55M FY2025 and ~1.5M FY2026) as Verizon pushes volume and SpaceX/Starlink Mobile and cable MVNOs compete -> YE 76.88M, avg 76.28M. 2028: net adds 1.0M -> avg 77.38M.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Bull: AT&T keeps ~1.5M net adds a year on convergence -> avg subs ~1% higher by 2028, ~+$0.25/share. Bear: net adds halve as Starlink Mobile and cable take share -> ~-1%.

inputs_detail.derivation: Base: FY2025 Advanced Connectivity wireless service revenue $67,384M (Q4 2025 Ex.99.4) / avg postpaid phone subs / 12. 2026: 9M wireless service $52,118M (Q3 2026 Ex.99.2) + Q4 est.; Q3 2026 call (postpaid phone ARPU +4%, new/refreshed plans, back-book pricing, promotions unchanged) | 2026: 9M $52,118M + Q4 at Q4-2025 $16,954M x 1.05 (Q3 2026 y/y growth 5.0%) = $69,920M / 74.95M / 12 = $77.74 (+1.7%). 2027 +1.5% to $78.91 (round 1: +0.6%): the Q3 call says postpaid phone ARPU grew 4% y/y from new and refreshed rate plans and back-book pricing, with promotions unchanged, and the 2026 price actions carry into H1 2027 before they lap; we stay below the supervisor's +1.75% because Verizon is buying volume and SpaceX/Starlink Mobile pricing pressure builds into its targeted end-2027 launch. 2028 +0.8% to $79.54 (round 1 +0.4%).
inputs_detail.variant_view: Bear: a price war (SpaceX pricing as a 4th network, Verizon promotions) takes all-in ARPU 2.5% below this path: ~-$1.8B revenue and EBIT a year, about -$1.9/share across the legs. Bull: price-ups stick (+1%), ~+$0.75/share. Supervisor reading +1.75% in 2027: ~+$0.2/share.

inputs_detail.derivation: Sep-30-2025 12,565k and Sep-30-2026 16,248k connections; Q3 2025 net adds 613k; 9M 2026 net adds 1,999k (Q3 2026 Ex.99.2) | Base = mid-2025 level as the FY2025 average: Sep-2025 12,565k less Q3-2025 net adds 613k = 11,952k. 2026: Dec-25 ~13.08M (Sep-25 + est. Q4-25 net adds ~0.52M), +~1.17M Lumen customers 2 Feb 2026 (16,248 - 1,999 - 13,080), quarter-ends 14.85/15.48/16.25M, Dec-26 ~16.95M (Q4 net adds ~0.70M) -> time-weighted average 15.44M (Lumen from 2 Feb: Q1 avg ~14.13, Q2 15.17, Q3 15.87, Q4 16.60; gate arithmetic fix of 15.55). 2027: net adds 2.5M (Q3 2026 run-rate 769k/quarter, fiber build to 60M+ locations by 2030) -> avg 18.2M; 2028: net adds 2.4M -> avg 20.65M.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Fiber net adds could slow as Lumen-territory penetration builds and fixed-wireless capacity fills; 10% fewer connections in 2028 is ~-$1.5B revenue, ~-$1.1/share.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2025 advanced home internet revenue $9,410M (Q4 2025 Ex.99.4); 9M 2026 $8,700M, Q3 2026 $2,975M (Q3 2026 Ex.99.2); call: fiber ARPU -4% y/y in Q3 with similar Q4 (Lumen Quantum mix, intro pricing, convergence discounts); Q3 2026 call transcript (Q4 fiber ARPU decline similar to Q3; relatively stable ARPU over the period) | Base $9,410M / 11.952M / 12 = $65.61. 2026: 9M $8,700M + Q4 est. $3,065M = $11,765M / 15.44M / 12 = $63.50 (-3.2%; gate fix of the connection average, the -4% fiber ARPU the call cited). 2027 $62.42 (-1.0%; round 1 +0.7%): the CFO expects Q4 2026 fiber ARPU down y/y at about the Q3 rate and "relatively stable ARPU" over 2026-28 with growth from customer additions, not pricing, so the Q4 exit rate sits below the 2026 average and Internet Air (lower ARPU) keeps growing in the mix. 2028 $62.73 (+0.5%).
inputs_detail.variant_view: If the -4% fiber ARPU trend persists through 2027 (convergence discounts, intro pricing), 2028 ARPU ~$59 instead of $62.7: ~-$0.9B revenue, ~-$0.8/share. Upside: tiered intro pricing rolls to rack rate, +2%/yr.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2025 AC revenue $112,424M and operating income $24,588M (Q4 2025 Ex.99.4); 9M 2026 AC operating income $21,826M, EBITDA $35,920M, D&A $14,094M (Q3 2026 Ex.99.3); $4B annual cost savings by end-2028 and copper retirement plan (Q3 call) | Set so AC EBIT = AC EBITDA - AC D&A. 2026: EBITDA $47,327M (+6.2% vs FY2025 $44,547M; 9M $35,920M + Q4 $11,407M), less D&A ~$18,800M = EBIT $28,527M. 2027: AC EBITDA +6.0% to $50,167M (round 1 +5.5%; the higher ARPU path adds ~$0.4B of revenue, of which we keep ~$0.24B after higher retention/marketing spend), less D&A $18,950M = $31,217M. 2028: +6.0% to $53,177M less D&A $19,350M = $33,827M. Cost = driver revenue - EBIT: $89,500M / $91,630M / $93,094M. Inside the "mid-to-high-single-digit" AC EBITDA guide (guidance_check).
inputs_detail.variant_view: If the $4B cost-out slips a year, 2028 AC cost is ~$1.5B higher: ~-$1.4/share. If the higher ARPU path all falls to EBITDA (no extra retention spend), 2027 AC EBITDA +6.4%: ~+$0.15/share.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2025 capex $20,842M (F51) + vendor financing $1,181M (Q4 2025 Ex.99.2) = $22.0B; 9M 2026 capital investment $16,786M (Q3 2026 Ex.99.3); guide $23-24B 2026, $22-23B 2027-28 (Q3 2026 release) | 2026: 9M $16,786M + Q4 ~$6.6B = $23.4B (inside the $23-24B guide). 2027 $22.7B and 2028 $22.6B: inside the lowered $22-23B guide, upper half because the record (2024 $22.1B vs $21-22B guide) runs slightly above and fiber build plus the Lumen footprint stays heavy. See guidance_check.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Spectrum (upper C-band) is not capital investment: carried as a separate probability-weighted adjustment (-$5B x 0.35).

inputs_detail.derivation: Today on our basis: EV $305.4B (mcap $20.93 x 6,746M = $141.2B + net debt $149.8B + NCI $18.0B + preferred $2.95B - Mexico 0.9 x $3.2B - fiber stake $3.65B) / NTM EBITDA $48.8B (0.19 x FY2026 $48.2B + 0.81 x FY2027 $48.9B) = 6.26x. Peers (CY2027E, after leases): median 5.52x, 5.98x ex-DT, VZ 6.17x, TMUS 5.98x, BCE 6.27x, RCI 6.47x; AT&T 5.78x on that basis. 6.2x keeps the whole post-2026-10-08 SpaceX de-rating (pre-news ~6.8x) and a little more for the end-2027 Starlink Mobile launch and Legacy EBITDA turning negative; ~5.85x on the peers' EV basis sits inside the range between the median and the ex-DT median.
inputs_detail.variant_view: A revert to the pre-news 6.8x adds ~+$4.7/share on this leg; the bear 5.3x takes ~-$7.1/share.

inputs_detail.derivation: driver_build.set: 149,819 - Q4-2026 FCF ~6,000 (call: ~$6B) - Jan-Oct 2027 FCF (FY2027 FCF less a seasonal Q4 ~6,100; = 12,837, 68% of the year) + dividends 1,880 (Q4-26) + 5,330 (three 2027 payments at $0.2775 x ~6.4B sh) + buybacks 2,700 (Q4-26, to ~$10B for 2026) + 5,600 (2027 to Oct) + NCI distributions ~1,400 = 147,892. Round 1 also added ~$650M separation cash on top: removed, because the $800M separation cash is already inside 2027 FCF (call: "will impact cash primarily in 2027"). Mexico, the fiber stake and spectrum are adjustments. Gate fix: 2027 FCF in the formula carries other EBIT -1,240 (was -1,580).
10-Q balance sheet: noncontrolling interest $15,979M + redeemable NCI $2,006M (mostly preferred interests in subsidiaries; NCI share of income $1,113M 9M 2026).

Series A 48,000 and Series C 70,000 shares outstanding (10-Q) x $25,000 liquidation preference per share (depositary shares of 1/1000th at $25) = $2,950M; consistent with preferred dividends of ~$36M a quarter (10-Q). Supervisor check: Series A 48,000 and Series C 70,000 shares x $25,000 liquidation preference = $2,950M; the Sep-2026 preferred dividend declaration reconciles.

10-Q R17: "We expect to receive approximately $2,000 in cash at closing" + $1,209M Mexico HFS finance leases that sit in net debt today (Ex.99.3) and leave with the business. Probability 0.9 for Mexican approval. Mexico EBITDA leaves the build after Q1 2027. Mexico HFS net assets are only ~$0.5B (R17: ~6,400 assets, ~5,900 liabilities).

10-Q R63 (discontinued operations, Lumen Mass Markets): total assets $4,781M - total liabilities $723M = $4,058M. Round 1 carried $2.58B by subtracting an assumed ~$2.0B Mexico net-asset figure from the combined held-for-sale totals ($11,216M - $6,636M); R63 isolates the fiber business, so that split was wrong. x 0.9: 50% is sold to GIP/CPP with Gigapower into a JV closing H1 2027 at undisclosed terms and AT&T keeps a non-controlling 50%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At full book (+$406M) +$0.06/share; at the round-1 $2.58B -$0.17/share.

inputs_detail.derivation: Auction 115 (160 MHz, 3.98-4.14 GHz) is scheduled to begin 2027-04-27 (Jones Walker) under the 2027-07-04 statutory deadline, with AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile expected to participate (Phillips Lytle). Judgment: AT&T wins a meaningful block for ~$5B (the 280 MHz C-band auction raised ~$81B, AT&T then ~$23B for 80 MHz; it already added EchoStar 3.45 GHz in 2025-26, so it needs less), and 0.35 that it is paid at that scale before 2027-10-23. Probability-weighted -$1.75B.
inputs_detail.variant_view: If SpaceX bids prices up and AT&T spends ~$10B: a further -$0.5/share; if AT&T sits out, +$0.27/share.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 8.1x NTM adjusted EPS $2.92 (driver-linked: FY2027 $2.64, FY2028 $2.98; Zacks $2.54/$2.86) + adjustments per share $0.75

inputs_detail.derivation: Today 8.1x on our NTM EPS ($20.93 / $2.59 = 0.19 x 2026 $2.38 + 0.81 x 2027 $2.64) and 8.3x on Zacks consensus ($2.51). Round 1 used 8.5x (VZ level); the supervisor noted it was the richest of the five without new evidence, and we found none, so we hold today's multiple. The ~23% discount to the 12-peer median 10.55x is structural: ~$1.6B a year of NCI and preferred claims ahead of common, 3.1x leverage, and US incumbents trade below the European/Canadian names (VZ 8.51x, CMCSA 7.4x).
inputs_detail.variant_view: At 8.5x (round 1) the P/E leg is +$1.2/share; at the VZ CY2027E 8.51x the same.

inputs_detail.derivation: driver_build.set: EPS_y = ((AC EBIT_y + other EBIT_y - interest_y + other income_y) x 0.78 - NCI $1,490M - preferred $144M) / avg shares; AC EBIT from the drivers; other EBIT (Legacy + LatAm + corporate) -$1,240M / -$2,190M (gate fix: corporate D&A no longer deducted twice); other income (pension/OPEB credits) $2,300M / $2,200M; avg shares 6,460M / 6,150M. FY2027 $2.64, FY2028 $2.98; NTM = 0.19 x FY2027 + 0.81 x FY2028 = $2.92. Zacks $2.54 / $2.86 -> NTM $2.80: we are ~4% higher on faster buybacks.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At consensus EPS ($2.80) the P/E leg is ~-$0.95/share.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 2026 interest $1,979M x 4 = $7.9B run-rate on $159.6B gross debt. 2027 and 2028 each raised $100M vs round 1 (call: higher cash interest from higher gross debt and rates; ~$10-15B a year refinanced above the ~4.95% average coupon); 2028 $7.9B, a little lower as net debt drifts down.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At a +50bp higher marginal rate on refinancing, 2028 interest ~+$0.1B: ~-$0.02 EPS.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 12.3% yield on NTM FCF/share $2.89 (driver-linked: FCF $18.9B FY2027 / $20.2B FY2028 after vendor financing, less NCI distributions and preferred dividends) + adjustments per share $0.75

inputs_detail.derivation: Today 12.3% on our NTM FCF to common ((0.19 x FY2026 $18.1B + 0.81 x FY2027 $18.9B - $1.45B NCI/preferred) / 6,746M = $2.57 / $20.93). Round 1 used 12.0% (a slight re-rating); held at today's 12.3% instead (supervisor finding; no new evidence for a re-rating).
inputs_detail.variant_view: At 12.0% the FCF leg is +$0.6/share; at the bear ~13.8%, about -$2.6/share.

inputs_detail.input: NTM FCF per share at the horizon (driver-linked)
inputs_detail.derivation: driver_build.set: FCF_y = adj. EBITDA_y - capital investment_y - K_y, EBITDA = AC EBIT (drivers) + other EBIT + D&A ($18,040M / $17,490M for the non-AC EBIT plus total D&A, after the gate fix of corporate EBIT), K = $7,280M (2027) and $8,226M (2028): cash interest, cash taxes (OBBBA benefit fades after 2027: ~+$0.95B in 2028), the ~$800M separation cash mainly in 2027 (call), device working capital and pension. FCF $18,937M / $20,151M; NTM = 0.19 x 2027 + 0.81 x 2028 - NCI distributions $1,310M - preferred dividends $144M = $18,466M / 6,385M shares = $2.89.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At the guide floors ($19B / $21B) FCF/share is ~$3.00: +$0.2/share on the FCF leg.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Cross-check only: dividend $1.11/share (maintained, Q3 release) at a 5.5% yield = $20.2; at 5.0% = $22.2. The dividend alone supports roughly today's price.

inputs_detail.derivation: Quarterly $0.2775 x 4 (declaration of 2026-09-24).
AT&T yields 5.3% today ($1.11 / $20.93); 5.5% assumes a slightly higher dividend-risk premium at 3.1x leverage.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Cross-check only: 12-peer CY2027E median P/E 10.55x x consensus NTM EPS $2.80 (Zacks blend) = $29.5. Not used: the median is lifted by European/Canadian names with lower leverage and no NCI/preferred claims; AT&T has not traded at the peer median in the past decade.

inputs_detail.derivation: Median of the 12 comps' CY2027E P/Es (10.5x TMUS and 10.6x BCE straddle it). Indicative only: MarketScreener does not state GAAP vs adjusted EPS for the set (gate mixed_basis); not used to set the P/E multiple.
Zacks consensus via the Nasdaq API: 0.19 x FY2027 $2.54 + 0.81 x FY2028 $2.86 = $2.80.

agents.reasoning: Round 2 (supervisor fact-checks plus a direct read of the AT&T Q3 call transcript, 10-Q R63/R17 and FCC auction notes). Evidence: Q3 2026 revenue $32.3B (+5.3%), adj. EBITDA $12.5B (+5.4%), adj. EPS $0.65, FCF ~$5.0B; 379k postpaid phone adds, churn 0.92%; postpaid phone ARPU +4% from new/refreshed plans and back-book pricing with promotions unchanged (call); fiber ARPU -4% with Q4 similar and "relatively stable ARPU" over 2026-28 (CFO). GAAP EPS $0.12-0.13 carries a $2.6B Mexico impairment and an ~$800M separation charge whose cash lands mainly in 2027. agents.reasoning: Round 2 rebuild after the supervisor's review. Facts fixed: fiber stake now +4,058 x 0.9 as an equity adjustment (R63; round 1 had ~$1.7B in net debt); net debt at the horizon re-derived at 145.4B (Q4 FCF ~6B, 68% of FY27 FCF by Oct-23, three dividends, ~$7B/yr buybacks, NCI/preferred, Mexico x0.9); FCF per share on horizon shares (6,385M); postpaid phone base on reported year-end counts (73.4815M); home-internet FY26 average time-weighted for the Lumen subscribers (14.06M), which lowers fiber ARPU to the -4% the company reports. Model deepened: a sixth driver, the AC EBITDA margin, now sets segment EBIT, and the P/E and FCF legs read EPS and FCF computed from the drivers; Legacy is a plain run-off segment (driven revenue 81%). Industry follow-ups (8 searches/fetches): Verizon steering to the top of its 750k-1M phone-add guide with no free phones (TIKR), Comcast blaming fiber's $30-40 gig pricing for its losses, SpaceX's own plan of rooftop small cells rather than macro towers (Wireless Estimator), and FCC rules forcing the upper C-band auction to close by July 2027 (Light Reading). So we moved 2027 wireless ARPU to +1.6% (from +2.0%, a little below the supervisor's +1.75%), 2027 adds to 1.0M, AC EBITDA to +6.0%/+5.25% (inside the guide, below the 9M +7.0% that Lumen flatters), FCF to $18.7B/$20.1B (just under the floors), and added -$5B x 0.35 for C-band. Peers are the supervisor's 12 incumbents on one CY2027E after-lease basis (median 5.52x, 5.98x ex-DT; P/E 10.55x); our 6.0x on our EV is ~5.58x on that basis and 8.0x P/E matches AT&T today. Research target (12m) $22.24 (round 1 $22.31; supervisor $23.29: we are lower on EBITDA and multiples). Scenarios bear $16.31 / base $22.24 / bull $27.51 at 25/50/25 with 17% within-scenario spread; the ladder shrinks the engine's median (~$22.0) toward spot for post-shock momentum and the SpaceX headline skew, median ~$21.6. Not driver-linked: none (all legs read the drivers); constants in the EPS/FCF expressions are listed in inputs_detail.

They enter the ladder as a separate component, not through the scenarios: a lognormal with median $21.13 (20.93 x exp(0.4 x ln 0.946 + 0.6 x ln 1.054) = 20.93 x 1.0094) and sigma 0.262 (pooled p10/p90 spread / 2.563), weight 0.30. Event odds: Polymarket SpaceX US carrier 13% by mid-2027 / 34.5% by end-2027 (thin, ~$15k, cross-check only); Fed cut by March 2027 14%. 7) Sources: ~half are company filings/releases and the brief-mandated peer pages (data); the discretionary ones are mostly in lane (Yahoo base-rate studies, Polymarket, FRED, FCC/Auction 107/AWS-3 history, new-entrant precedents). memo.title: AT&T (T) Long: SpaceX de-rating priced in, cash path intact - target $22.65, research target (12m) $23.16 plus a 5.3% yield
memo.call_reason: The published target ($22.65) is above the $20.93 price and conviction is medium (rubric), with a 5.3% dividend on top and a stop at $16.54 that sits on the $16.5 thesis-break level.
memo.one_liner: AT&T lost ~16% in October on SpaceX headlines (Grain 800 MHz licences, a reported 80,000-site push) while Q3 beat and 2026 EPS was raised; our horizon multiples keep that de-rating and still value the shares at a research target (12m) of $23.16 (+10.6%) on the earnings path alone. We buy 167 shares at or below the page's Entry below (~$21.60), ahead of this week's peer prints and the Oct-29 FCC vote, stop $16.54, take-profit $27.52.

thesis.point: Earnings power is rising, not falling: EPS growth from lower D&A and ~5% a year of buybacks carries value even at today's de-rated multiples.
thesis.evidence: Q3 2026 revenue $32.3B (+5.3%), adjusted EBITDA $12.5B (+5.4%), adjusted EPS $0.65; 2026 EPS guide raised to ~$2.40, mainly on lower depreciation from held-for-sale accounting for Mexico. Our driver build gives adjusted EPS $2.66 (2027) and $2.91 (2028) vs Zacks consensus $2.54 / $2.86; at 8.3x (AT&T's own NTM P/E today) the P/E leg alone is $24.01.

thesis.point: The October drawdown is a multiple event, and we keep it in the target rather than betting on a rebound.
thesis.evidence: Closes fell 24.87 -> 22.18 (-10.8%) on Oct-9 (SpaceX buys Grain's 800 MHz licences), 23.42 -> 21.91 (-6.4%) on results day Oct-21, and 22.74 -> 20.93 (-8.0%) on Oct-23 (Bloomberg: SpaceX seeks 80,000+ sites). The horizon EV/EBITDA stays at the post-news 6.1x (~$2.8/sh of de-rating retained; 6.1x = 5.69x on the peer basis vs an 11-incumbent median of 5.98x ex-DT). SpaceX targets next-generation service by end-2027, so most fourth-carrier cash-flow damage falls after our 2027-10-23 horizon.

thesis.point: Cash returns and asset sales put a floor under the equity.
thesis.evidence: $0.2775 quarterly dividend (5.3% yield at $20.93), $24B+ of buybacks guided for 2026-28, Mexico sale for ~$2.0B cash at closing (Q1 2027) and a 50% fiber JV stake carried at $4,058M (taken at x0.9 = +$3.65B). At the $16.5 thesis break the stock would yield 6.7% and ~15% FCF-to-common at ~5.2x EBITDA on the peer basis, a level consistent only with a broken cash path.

memo.variant_view: We sit between the Street and the options market. Sell-side (24 analysts, Buy) has a median target of $28.00 (mean $27.80, range $20-34), roughly 21% above our research target (12m) of $23.16: we keep the post-SpaceX 6.1x EV/EBITDA and model FCF of $18.5B / $19.9B for 2027-28, below both management's $19B+ / $21B+ floors and consensus ($19.24B / $20.97B), because Legacy EBITDA turns negative after 2027 and wireless ARPU growth fades to +0.75% in 2028. The options market is more bearish than we are: its standalone 12-month median is $21.35 with P(gain) 52.7%, vs our published 60.2%. Our variant view is therefore narrow and specific: EPS (above consensus on lower D&A and buybacks) carries value at a de-rated multiple, so we do not need the SpaceX fear to fade to make money; a move back toward the pre-October ~6.8x would add ~$2.8/sh on top. This is not a large mispricing call; most of the expected return is the dividend plus a modest earnings-path gain.

valuation.methods: Research target (12m) $23.16 = model-engine base horizon value (23.1576) of the supervisor's reconciled driver set (wireless and fiber subs x ARPU, Advanced Connectivity margin, capital investment ~$23.4B/22.8B/22.7B): EV/EBITDA 6.1x on NTM EBITDA ~$50.4B = $22.55 (weight 0.5), P/E 8.3x on driver-linked NTM EPS $2.86 = $24.01 (0.35), 12.3% FCF yield on $2.82/share = $23.19 (0.15); net debt at horizon $144.3B, NCI $18.0B, preferred $2.95B, fiber stake +$3.65B, expected upper C-band spend -$2.0B (-$5B x 0.4), 6,387M shares. No DCF leg (not in the DCF policy for this sector). The five forecasters' values span $22.24-24.39. The published target $22.65 is the median of the final distribution, which blends the options market (weight 0.67, median $21.35) with the research ladder (0.33); expected value $23.42 (+11.9%), P(gain) 60.2%. Bear values $15.15-16.68 (price war, cable-like ~5.2-5.3x), bull values $27.51-29.23 (re-rating toward ~6.8-7.0x).

catalysts.event: Verizon Q3 2026 results (out today)
catalysts.why_it_moves: First big read on wireless pricing after the SpaceX news; Verizon has been buying share. It reported 406k postpaid phone net adds (vs 44k a year ago, and above AT&T's 379k), raised its 2026 phone-add guide to 1.1-1.2M and cut promotional acquisition cost 41% y/y.
catalysts.watch: Whether share gains came from price (bad for T) or lower subsidies (good for industry pricing); any call comment on SpaceX or satellite; T's reaction vs VZ today.

catalysts.event: FOMC rate decisions
catalysts.why_it_moves: A 5.3%-yield, 3.1x-levered stock trades partly as a bond proxy; the forecasters flagged a ~5% 10-year yield and few cuts priced as a cap on yield-stock multiples.
catalysts.watch: 10-year Treasury yield after each decision; a dovish turn helps the multiple, a hawkish one hurts it.

catalysts.why_it_moves: Second wireless read-across in three days and T-Mobile's SpaceX commentary (it is SpaceX's existing direct-to-cell partner); TMUS fell more than T on the SpaceX headlines.
catalysts.watch: Postpaid phone adds and churn, promotional intensity, any statement on SpaceX site access or wholesale talks.

catalysts.why_it_moves: Widening satellite access to terrestrial bands lowers the barrier for Starlink Mobile; AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile have lobbied to keep carrier consent and to exclude 2.5/3.45 GHz. Agenda items are tentative until the meeting.
catalysts.watch: Whether the adopted NPRM keeps carrier consent and which bands are proposed; it is a proposal, not a final rule.

catalysts.event: Charter Q3 2026 results
catalysts.why_it_moves: Broadband and cable-MVNO read-across: cable losses to fiber support AT&T fiber adds, but cable has called fiber pricing 'irrational' and AT&T fiber ARPU fell 4% in Q3.
catalysts.watch: Charter broadband net losses, mobile line adds, pricing response to fiber overbuild.

catalysts.event: Any signed SpaceX cell-site access deal (Bloomberg-reported talks for 80,000+ sites)
catalysts.why_it_moves: A signed deal is the step that turns a satellite service into a terrestrial fourth carrier; each SpaceX headline this month cost T 8-11% in a day.
catalysts.watch: Tower-company announcements, site counts and lease terms; any SpaceX US pricing; any wholesale or partner deal with an incumbent instead (would be +).

catalysts.event: Quarterly dividend declaration (last year on 2025-12-15; record date ~mid-Jan 2027)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Confirms the $0.2775 payout that underpins the 5.3% yield; a hold is expected, any change would be a major signal.
catalysts.watch: Amount held at $0.2775; any new buyback authorization alongside.

catalysts.event: AT&T Q4 2026 results and 2027 outlook (first print under the new CFO from 2027-01-01; last year's Q4 print was 2026-01-28)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The single biggest scheduled event: management promised more color on the 2027 FCF bridge to $19B+; we model $18.5B, so a firm bridge is upside and a soft one confirms our below-floor view.
catalysts.watch: 2027 FCF guide vs $19B+, capital investment $22-23B, buyback pace vs $24B+ 2026-28, Q4 postpaid phone adds vs Q3's 379k, fiber ARPU (guided ~-4% in Q4), separation cash.

catalysts.event: Mexico wireless sale closes (~$2.0B cash at closing)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Cash to net debt and leases leave the balance sheet; small but supports the deleveraging story.
catalysts.watch: Closing announcement and proceeds vs ~$2.0B.

catalysts.event: FCC review and closing of SpaceX's purchase of Grain's 800 MHz licences (expected H1 2027)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Approval with terrestrial flexibility would firm up the fourth-carrier case; conditions or delay would ease it.
catalysts.watch: FCC conditions on terrestrial use, carrier petitions, closing date.

catalysts.event: AT&T Q1 2027 results (Q1 2026 was reported 2026-04-22)
catalysts.why_it_moves: First quarter of 2027 pricing and the Legacy decline; tests whether ARPU growth holds once 2026 price actions lap.
catalysts.watch: Postpaid phone ARPU growth vs our +1.6% for 2027, churn vs 0.92%, Q1 FCF seasonality.

catalysts.event: FCC Auction 115 (upper C-band, 160 MHz) bidding
catalysts.why_it_moves: We carry -$5B x 0.4 = -$2.0B (-$0.31/sh); heavy AT&T bidding at 3.13x leverage would hit net debt before the horizon and could slow buybacks.
catalysts.watch: Qualified-bidder list, AT&T commentary on participation, SpaceX as a bidder.

catalysts.why_it_moves: Crystallises the fiber stake we carry at +$3.65B and brings proceeds for debt reduction.
catalysts.watch: Proceeds (undisclosed so far) and any payments AT&T owes the JV for network access.

risks.risk: SpaceX becomes a priced, national fourth carrier (Grain 800 MHz + EchoStar spectrum + leased terrestrial sites); supervisor probability 0.35 over 2028-2031, and the market can price it well before then (bear values $15.15-16.68).
risks.signpost: A signed site-lease deal for tens of thousands of towers; FCC approval of the Grain licences with terrestrial rights; a US price list for Starlink Mobile; Polymarket odds of a US carrier by end-2027 rising from 34.5% (thin market).

risks.risk: Free cash flow misses the floors and buybacks slow: we already sit below management ($18.5B vs $19B+ in 2027), and the 2025 tax-law cash benefit runs off after 2027.
risks.signpost: Q4 print guides 2027 FCF below $19B or capital investment above $23B; buyback pace below the ~$24B+ 2026-28 plan.

risks.risk: Wireless price competition: Verizon is taking share (406k Q3 phone adds, guide raised to 1.1-1.2M) while AT&T adds slowed to 379k; fiber ARPU is already -4% y/y.
risks.signpost: AT&T postpaid phone adds below ~300k a quarter, churn above 1.0%, postpaid phone ARPU growth falling from +4% toward +1%, rising promotions on the Q4 call.

risks.risk: Balance sheet: 3.13x leverage with the 2.5x target pushed to 2029, a Fitch BBB+ Negative Outlook, $9.5B of debt due within a year and possible ~$5B upper C-band spend.
risks.signpost: A Fitch downgrade, AT&T qualifying to bid heavily in Auction 115, refinancing at materially higher coupons.

what_changes_our_mind: A signed SpaceX terrestrial site deal at national scale (tens of thousands of towers) or FCC approval of the Grain licences with full terrestrial flexibility before mid-2027: move to No position.
The late-January Q4 print guides 2027 FCF below $19B, slows the $24B+ buyback plan, or shows postpaid phone adds below ~300k with ARPU growth fading: exit.

Upside case: SpaceX talks end in a wholesale/partner deal with incumbents and AT&T holds +4% phone ARPU with adds back above 400k; the multiple can revert toward ~6.8x (~+$2.8/sh), so we would hold through the take-profit review rather than trim.

Inside the peer range 8.9-11.8x (IPP and all-peer median 10.6x), on the same pre-SBC consensus basis as peers. VST today ~9.8x NTM (EV $72.7B = 152.2 x 335.6M + 19,160 + 2,488 over ~$7.36B NTM = 0.2 x 7.2 + 0.8 x 7.4; ~9.5x pro forma for Cogentrix on $8.1B). 0.25x below today's pro forma level because the horizon NTM (Q4-27 to Q3-28) is ~79% FY2028, which is only ~72% hedged vs ~94% for 2027 with ERCOT forwards lower (source 3, 5), and the post-2029/30 PJM design (source 31) is 1-2 years nearer. Each 0.25x = ~$6.3/share.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FY2026-30 FCFF from revenue growth 10/11/5/4/3%, pre-SBC EBIT margin 26.2-27.2%, tax 21%, D&A 11-10.5%, capex 14% -> 11%; WACC 9.37%, g 2.5%; TV 82% of DCF; same equity bridge

inputs_detail.derivation: TTM revenue $18,985M (F6) is already +8% on FY2025; FY2027 adds Cogentrix (~5,500 MW, source 30) and Meta PPA volumes; slower growth after 2027. Revenue is mostly commodity pass-through, so margins are set to hit the EBITDA path below.

inputs_detail.input: Adjusted (pre-SBC) EBITDA path FY2026 / FY2027 / FY2028
inputs_detail.derivation: FY2026 = midpoint of the $6.8-7.6B guide (mgmt 'at or above the midpoint', sources 3, 5) = $7.2B; FY2027 = low end $7.4B (CFO 'trending towards the lower end') + ~$0.7B Cogentrix/Meta ('roughly $700 million', source 5) = $8.1B; FY2028 $8.5B = judgment: +5% on FY2027 for full-year Cogentrix/Meta and PJM, held below consensus because only ~72% of 2028 is hedged and ERCOT forwards are 'meaningfully lower' (sources 3, 5). Pre-SBC, matching Vistra's Ongoing Ops Adjusted EBITDA and the peers' consensus basis. Arithmetic: 7,200/19,345 = 37.2%; 8,100/21,473 = 37.7%; 8,500/22,546 = 37.7%.
FY2025 D&A $1,986M / revenue $17,586M = 11.3%; drifts down as revenue grows faster than the asset base, with Cogentrix adding assets in 2027.
Federal statutory 21%; TTM tax/pretax = 584/2,803 = 20.8%.
FY2025 capex $2,752M = 15.6% of revenue, TTM $2,866M; growth capex (Permian peakers, nuclear uprates, Oak Hill 2 solar) tapers after 2027.

inputs_detail.input: Net claims at horizon (net debt + preferred)
inputs_detail.derivation: Management capital plan (source 5) prorated over 2026-07-01 to 2027-10-14 (15.5 of 24 months = 0.646): available cash $10,000M ('more than $10 billion', taken at $10B) x 0.646 = -$6,460M; equity holders: $3,000M less H1-2026 buybacks $709M and dividends $154M (F67, F74 derivations) = $2,137M for H2-26 + 2027, x 15.5/18 = +$1,840M; growth other than Cogentrix and Helix: ($4,750M midpoint - $2,300M Cogentrix cash - $1,000M Helix) x 0.646 = +$937M; Helix capital calls +$500M (judgment: only the first $500M is unconditional and management 'cannot predict the amount or timing', source 5); Cogentrix cash $2,300M + assumed debt $1,500M = +$3,800M (sources 1, 30). 21,636 - 6,460 + 1,840 + 937 + 500 + 3,800 = 22,253 -> $22,250M. Whether the $1.5B junior notes replace Series A/B preferred (424B2 use of proceeds, source 6) does not change total claims.

335.6M cover count (F103) + 5.0M Cogentrix consideration shares (source 30) - $1.2B remaining authorization (to be exhausted no later than end-2027, running ahead of pro-rata, source 5) / ~$155 = -7.7M + SBC dilution ~1.0M = 333.9M.

Estimate: cost of equity 5.19% (10y, source 23) + beta 1.2 (judgment vs ~1.5x market sensitivity, source 26) x ERP 5% = 11.19%; after-tax cost of debt 6.5% (anchored on the 7.0-7.25% junior notes, source 6) x (1 - 21%) = 5.135%; market weights mcap ~$51B / claims ~$22B = 70/30; 0.70 x 11.19% + 0.30 x 5.135% = 9.37% (corrected from 9.25%, which used ~68/32 weights). [citation gate 2026-10-14]

Nominal long-run power demand growth: EIA commercial demand +2.8% in 2027 (source 20); AI capex base case rising through 2028 (source 25); held at 2.5% rather than higher because PJM's 2030/31+ capacity design is open and PJM cites retail-bill concerns (source 31).

agents.reasoning: Round 2. Anchor: 1y realized vol 50%, beta ~1.5; VST has traded from ~4-5x forward adj. EBITDA (pre-2024) to ~10-11x (2024-25 peaks) and ~9.8x NTM standalone today - base rates are context, not inputs. Fundamentals (company sources): 2026 adj. EBITDA guide $6.8-7.6B (at/above mid), 2027 trending to the $7.4B low end plus ~$0.7B Cogentrix/Meta = $8.1B; ~94% of 2027 and ~72% of 2028 hedged with ERCOT forwards lower; >$10B available cash 2026-27, ~$3B to equity holders, $4.5-5B growth incl. Cogentrix and Helix. Changes after the supervisor's review: (1) SBC counted once - pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA like the peers, SBC as ~1M shares of dilution; (2) multiple 9.0x -> 9.25x, now on the peers' basis; I stay 0.25x under VST's ~9.5x pro forma level because the horizon NTM is mostly the 72%-hedged 2028 and the post-2029/30 PJM design is nearer; (3) horizon claims $24.0B -> $22.25B, rebuilt from management's prorated capital plan with only $0.5B of Helix calls (timing unpredictable per the CFO); (4) shares 333.1M -> 333.9M; (5) +$0.63B Cogentrix tax-benefit NPV confirmed in Vistra's release; (6) P/E leg dropped because it rested on thin (1-2 analyst) FY2028 consensus. The preferred-refinancing claim is kept: the 424B2 use-of-proceeds section states it (the supervisor checked the 8-K, which does not), and total claims are unchanged either way. Fair value $160.5 (EV/EBITDA $168.3 x 0.7, DCF $142.2 x 0.3). PJM thesis-break status confirmed at PJM's ER26-1556 answer: collar through 2029/30 only, 2030/31+ path to be set after the end-2026 stakeholder review; not tripped. Today's -6.5% was macro/sector (hot CPI) and does not change value. Ladder: 25/50/25 lognormal mixture at the engine scenario values $108/$162/$211 with 27% within-scenario vol (total log-sd ~0.36, below the 50% realized vol because part of that is mean-reverting factor noise); median $158.1, P(>=152) = 0.54.

supervisor.confidence_reason: Round 2 settled the two remaining number-moving disagreements: the horizon claims bridge (now $22.9B, from the call's own allocation of the $10B), and the DCF gap. Every agent's DCF sits 15-27% below its multiple leg because three use 2.0% terminal growth that re-prices the PJM risk already in the multiple; fixing it lifts my fair value to $166.0 vs the $158.7 mean. That points the update up, but it is a method correction of ~2 points of probability at the centre, not a new fact about the business, so it is not 'high'.

changes.why: Exit k=0.8 rule (2026-10-26 12:16Z) not applied to VST: Kilian card 2026-10-26 15:02Z 'Keep the argued 9.0x' (alternatives were 9.21x on standalone EBITDA, own 9.01x, and 8.32x on FMP consensus, own 7.93x). The ERCOT/PJM discount case stands in for the rule. Rejected version kept as *.exitk-rejected.
Reconciled set: 9.5x on pre-SBC EBITDA ($172.5, 0.7) and a DCF at 9.0% / 2.5% ($150.9, 0.3) with horizon claims of $22.9B; the forecaster mean carries DCFs 15-27% below their own multiples.
Centre moved up ~$3 (median ~$154.5 -> ~$156.5), part of the way to the reconciled set's $162.5, for the DCF-terminal and claims-bridge corrections; the mean's left tail is kept.

changes.why: DCF check: 2.0% re-priced the post-2029/30 PJM risk already in the multiple discount, the flat FY2029-30 EBITDA and the bear case.
Built from FCFbG guidance (~$6.0B to the horizon) and the call's capital plan (~$3B equity incl. H1 paid, $4.5-5B growth, $2-2.5B unallocated).

changes.item: a fact agent_5 got wrong: 'more than $10 billion of available cash' prorated as cash generated
changes.why: The call allocates the $10B to equity, growth and ~$2-2.5B unallocated; FCFbG is ~$9.2B over 2026-27 (2026 guidance midpoint $4,325M + 2027 estimate ~$4,860M = 8,100 x 4,325/7,200) (cash generated to the horizon, $M).
The extra 0.25x restates the hedge/PJM reasons already in the 1.1x discount to the 10.6x IPP median.
~8.0x the $8.1B 2027 base on pro forma claims, ~0.9x below NRG; with a fundamental trigger attached.

supervisor.summary: Round 2 converged: all five now use the $8.1B 2027 base, pre-SBC EBITDA like the peers, the full Cogentrix cost and the verified tax NPV, with fair values of $154-163 (mean $158.7). Two corrections remain: horizon claims are ~$22.9B when built from FCFbG guidance and the call's capital plan, and the DCFs sit 15-27% below the multiples mainly because 2.0% terminal growth re-prices the PJM risk the 9.5x multiple already carries. With 2.5% terminal growth my reconciled fair value is $166.0 (DCF $150.9, -12.5% vs the multiple; WACC 9.0% vs 8.4% implied), so I nudge the ladder up ~2 points at the centre with medium confidence. The PJM post-2029/30 cap flag is open, not tripped; thesis break $115.

fair_value.reason: Model update 2026-10-23 (update): peer set refresh (Kilian 2026-10-26 06:07Z); the IPP-only peer median fell from 10.6x to 10.06x NTM EV/EBITDA on the 10-23 close, so the horizon multiple moves 9.5x -> 9.0x with the same 1.1x discount, and the engine value of the set goes from $159.66 to $147.67 (-7.5%). Nothing else in the set changed. No-DCF rule (Kilian 2026-10-21 13:50Z: no DCF leg for any researched name except the neoclouds), applied 2026-10-22: the engine re-run of the reconciled set without its 0.3 DCF leg gives $172.53 (runs/2026-10-14/VST/model_engine.json model_fair_value; was $166.03 with the DCF at $150.9). Original reason: Engine base horizon value of the reconciled set: 9.5x horizon NTM pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA ($8.42B = 0.21 x FY2027 $8.1B + 0.79 x FY2028 $8.5B) less $20.4B net debt and $2.49B preferred/NCI, plus $0.63B Cogentrix tax NPV, over 334.6M shares = $172.5 (weight 0.7); DCF at 9.0% WACC and 2.5% terminal growth = $150.9 (0.3). Changes from round 1 ($160.8): horizon net debt $20.8B -> $20.4B (FCFbG to the horizon ~$6.0B, distributions ~$1.84B from the call's $3B plan) and terminal growth 2.0% -> 2.5% (the DCF check; PJM risk counted once).
